20020409035729I	(.23) NOTIFIED BY O'HARE CITY OPERATIONS OF THE FOLLOWING INCIDENT: AN AMERICAN AIRLINES FOKKER-100, N1411G, FLIGHT 1949, BLEW FOUR MAIN LANDING GEAR TIRES DURING LANDING ON RUNWAY 09R AT APPROXIMATELY 08:53 AM ON THE 9 APRIL 02. THE AIRCRAFT LANDED ON RUNWAY 09R THE DUMP LIFTERS AND THRUST REVERSERS DID NOT DEPLOY, THE BRAKES WERE APPLIED AND ALL FOUR MAIN LANDING GEAR TIRES BLEW. PASSENGERS AND CREW ABOARD THE AIRCRAFT WERE DEPLANED THROUGH THE FORWARD ENTRY DOOR VIA MOBILE STAIRS AND BUSSED TO THE TERMINAL NO INJURIES WERE REPORTED. WHEN INSPECTOR RAUPP, OLIVER AND HILL ARRIVED ON THE SCENE THE PIC TERRY BURLINGAME (201427826) AND F/O JOHN CATURIA (474605767) WERE NOT AT THE AIRCRAFT. THE DAMAGED AIRCRAFT AND LOGBOOK WERE INSPECTED. DURING OUR INITIAL INVESTIGATION, WE DISCOVERED THAT THE ANTI-SKID SYSTEM HAD BEEN PLACARDED ON (04-09-02) PER MEL (32-2, 4-138D0-C) ON LOGBOOK PAGE NUMBER (7051072). PHOTOGRAPHS WERE TAKEN OF THE LOGBOOK PLACARD, AIRCRAFT'S FINAL LOCATION ON RUNWAY 09R, AND CONDITION OF THE LEFT AND RIGHT LANDING GEAR TIRES. AFTER COMPLETING OUR AIRCRAFT INSPECTION WE OBSERVED TIRE DEBRIS AND TWO SETS OF TIRE SKID MARKS ALIGNED WITH THE AIRCRAFT AT M-3 AND "F" TAXIWAY MARKERS. RUNWAY 9R WAS CLOSED AT APPROXIMATELY 08:53 AM, THE AIRCRAFT WAS TOWED AND 9R REOPENED AT APPROXIMATELY 11:48 AM ON 9 APR. 02. INSPECTOR RAUPP, OLIVER, AND HILL WENT TO AALA OPERATIONS TO GET STATEMENTS FROM THE PIC AND F/O BOTH DECLINED AND STATED THEY WOULD INCLUDE THEIR STATEMENTS IN THE AVIATION SAFETY ACTION PROGRAM (ASAP) REPORT. INSPECTOR RAUPP CONTACTED ROBERT TALMADGE POI FOR AALA TO REQUEST CREW HISTORY AND CAPTAINS REPORT AND ALL AVAILABLE INFORMATION CONCERNING THIS INCIDENT. THE INFORMATION REQUESTED FROM AALA WAS RECEIVED ON 15 APRIL 2002 ALONG WITH AN OPERATIONAL SYNOPSIS FROM AALA T.J. AHERN VICE PRESIDENT SAFETY, SECURITY AND ENVIRONMENTAL WHICH STATED FLIGHT 1949 DEPARTED MSP WITH THE ANTI-SKID PLACARDED INOPERATIVE. THE CAPTAIN WAS FLYING. THE FLIGHT LANDED AT ORD ON RUNWAY 09R. THE TOUCHDOWN WAS NORMAL AND IN THE TOUCHDOWN ZONE. THE LIFT DUMPERS AND THRUST REVERSERS DID NOT DEPLOY. THE BRAKES WERE APPLIED IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE F100 OPERATING MANUAL. THE BRAKES APPEARED TO LOCK UP AND A SKID DEVELOPED. THE AIRCRAFT CAME TO A STOP NEAR THE M6 INTERSECTION ON RUNWAY 09R. INVESTIGATION REVEALED ALL FOUR TIRES WERE DEFLATED. PASSENGERS WERE DEPLANED NORMALLY THROUGH THE FORWARD ENTRY DOOR VIA MOBILE STAIRS AND BUSSED TO THE AALA TERMINAL. AFTER REVIEWING THE AALA SYNOPSIS A FOLLOW-UP INVESTIGATION WAS PERFORMED TO OBTAIN INFORMATION ON STATUS OF THE DISCREPANCIES NOTED IN THE AALA SYNOPSIS. CONTACTED AALA MAINTENANCE MANAGER LAUDICINA WHO PROVIDED COPIES OF LOGBOOK PAGES (7081073 THRU 7081075) WHICH IDENTIFIED DISCREPANCIES, COMPLETED CORRECTIVE ACTIONS AND REQUIRED OPS CHECKS FOR THE ANTI-SKID, BLOWN TIRES/WHEELS, WITH ONE EXCEPTION, THERE WAS NO DISCREPANCY ON THE THRUST REVERSERS FAILURE TO DEPLOY. AT THAT TIME MAINTENANCE MANAGER LAUDICINA RAN A MAINTENANCE HISTORY ON THIS AIRCRAFT TO DETERMINE IF A THRUST REVERSER PROBLEM HAD BEEN REPORTED SINCE THIS INCIDENT OCCURRED. NO DISCREPANCY WAS FOUND WHICH IDENTIFIED A PROBLEM WITH THE OPERATION OF THE THRUST REVERSERS. IN CONCLUSION THIS INVESTIGATION IDENTIFIED SOME CRITICAL ISSUES WHICH CLEARLY HAVE BEEN LEFT UNANSWERED. IT APPEARS FROM OUR INVESTIGATION THAT THIS AIRCRAFT COULD HAVE TOUCHED DOWN LONG ON RUNWAY 09R BASED ON THE TIRE MARKINGS ON THE RUNWAY, THE CREW WAS AWARE THAT THE ANTI-SKID SYSTEM WAS INOP. BASED ON THE PLACARDING AND THE LOGBOOK ENTRY BUT FAILED TO APPLY THE CORRECT BRAKING PROCEDURE FOR AN AIRCRAFT WITH AN INOP. ANTI-SKID SYSTEM. THE DUMP LIFTER SYSTEM WAS NEVER ACTIVATED BASED ON THE FACT THAT NO FAULTS WERE IDENTIFIED WHEN SYSTEM WAS OPS CHECKED. THE THRUST REVERSER SYSTEM WAS NEVER ACTIVATED ON LANDING ROLL BASED ON THE FACT THAT NO DISCREPANCE WAS EVER IDENTIFIED TO MAINTENANCE OR IN THE MAINTENANCE HISTORY. EACH OF THE ABOVE ISSUES ARE CRITICAL

THESE STATEMENTS ARE AVAILABLE FOR REVIEW AT THE FAA UNITED AIRLINES SAN FRANCISCO CERTIFICATE MANAGEMENT OFFICE (SFO-CMO). UAL FLIGHT 862, A B747-400, WAS A SCHEDULE FLIGHT FROM SIDNEY, AUSTRALIA TO SAN FRANCISCO, CA ON MAY 1, 2002. APPROXIMATELY 2.5 HOURS FROM, AND 1000 MILES NORTHEAST OF, SIDNEY, AUSTRALIA, THE FLIGHT EXPERIENCED SEVERE TURBULENCE, WHICH RESULTED IN INJURY TO TWO (2) FLIGHT ATTENDANTS AND FIVE (5) PASSENGERS. THE AIRCRAFT DIVERTED TO AUCKLAND, NEW ZEALAND AND MADE AN UNEVENTFUL LANDING. SOON AFTER COMPLETING THE MEAL SERVICE, AND WHILE PICKING UP THE REST OF THE REFUSE, THE CAPTAIN TURNED ON THE SEATBELT SIGNS. AS THE FLIGHT ATTENDANTS WERE MAKING THEIR WAY THROUGH THE CABIN TO ENSURE ALL THE PASSENGERS HAD BUCKLED THEIR SEATBELTS, THE CAPTAIN MADE AN ANNOUNCEMENT FOR THE FLIGHT ATTENDANTS TO TAKE THEIR SEATS AND FASTEN THEIR SEATBELTS. ALMOST IMMEDIATELY, THE AIRCRAFT ENCOUNTERED THE FIRST OF WHAT WAS TO BE SEVERAL MINUTES OF SEVERE TURBULENCE. ONCE CLEAR OF THE TURBULENCE, THE FLIGHT ATTENDANTS BEGAN THE TASK OF ACCESSING AND TREATING THE INJURED. THE CAPTAIN ANNOUNCED THEY WERE DIVERTING TO AUCKLAND, NEW ZEALAND WHERE THE AIRCRAFT LANDED UNEVENTFULLY. IN CONCLUSION, EACH STATEMENT BY THE CREW INDICATES THAT THE SEQUENCE OF EVENTS FROM THE CAPTAIN TURNING ON THE SEAT BELT SIGN, INSTRUCTING THE FLIGHT ATTENDANTS TO TAKE THEIR SEATS, AND THE FIRST OCCURRENCE OF TURBULENCE, ALL HAPPENED IN A VERY SHORT TIME. ONE CREWMEMBER INDICATED THAT THE TOTAL TIME WAS PROBABLY ONLY 10-15 SECONDS. EACH STATEMENT INDICATES THAT THERE WAS VERY LITTLE TIME TO PREPARE EVERYONE FOR WHAT WAS TO FOLLOW.

HE THEN FOLLOWED THEIR INSTRUCTIONS TO LEAVE THE AIRPORT TRAFFIC AREA AND PROCEEDED SOME 7-10 MILES NORTHWEST TO A VFR PRACTICE AREA. IN THE PRACTICE AREA HE WAS INSTRUCTED AS THE PROCEDURE FOR AN EMERGENCY GEAR EXTENSION. THE PILOT WAS ABLE TO GET "GREENS" ON THE MAIN GEAR ONLY, BUT DECIDED TO RETURN FOR LANDING IN THAT CONFIGURATION WHEN THE AIRPLANE BEGAN TO VIBRATE HEAVILY. THE NOSE GEAR ANNUNCIATOR DISPLAYED DOWN AND LOCKED AS THE PILOT MADE AN APPROACH FOR AN EMERGENCY LANDING ON RUNWAY 30. THE PILOT TAXIIED IN AS NORMAL, HOWEVER, THE PROPELLER TIPS WERE CURLED AFT 6-7 INCHES, THE TAIL TIE DOWN WAS GROUND DOWN ONE QUARTER INCH, AND THE RIGHT SIDE STEP SHOWED CONTACT WITH THE RUNWAY. THE MAIN TIRES WERE ABRAIDED OUTBOARD OF THE TREAD AREA AS IF THEY HAD BEEN APPLIED TO THE RUNWAY AT AN EXTREME ANGLE. THE GEAR DOORS WERE UNDAMAGED. MECHANICS LATER DETERMINED THAT THE ELECTRIC GEAR PUMP MOTOR WAS INOPERATIVE. NORTH LAS VEGAS AIR TRAFFIC CONTROL TOWER DID NOT REFER THIS EVENT TO FLIGHT STANDARDS AS AN INCIDENT. RATHER, IT WAS REPORTED TO ME BY THE CHIEF PILOT OF THE FLIGHT SCHOOL BY TELEPHONE, SAME DAY. THIS CHEROKEE ARROW HAS AN ELECTRICALLY CONTROLLED, HYDRAULICALLY ACTUATED RETRACTABLE GEAR SYSTEM. A UNIQUE FEATURE IS THAT THE LANDING GEAR WILL EXTEND AUTOMATICALLY IF THE PILOT FORGETS IT, AS A FUNCTION OF AIRSPEED AND THROTTLE POSITION. HOWEVER, THIS SYSTEM CAN BE OVERRIDDEN, OR DISABLED, DEPENDING ON THE POSITION OF A SMALL LEVER ON THE CONSOLE THAT HOUSES THE ELEVATOR TRIM (BETWEEN THE TWO FRONT SEATS). IN THIS CASE, THE GEAR MUST BE EXTENDED INTENTIONALLY IN THEUSUAL WAY. THE SUBJECT PILOT FLEW HIS TRIP AND RETURNED TO THE RUNWAY AT NORTH LAS VEGAS WITH THE AUTOMATIC SYSTEM DISABLED. NOTWITHSTANDING HIS REPRESENTATIONS TO THE CONTRARY, ON HIS ARRIVAL, HE EITHER FORGOT TO EXTEND THE GEAR, OR EXTENDED IT IN GROUND EFFECT. THE GEAR STOPPED AT ABOUT 45-50 DEGREES AND STAYED THERE UNTIL HE MANUALLY EXTENDED THE GEAR IN THE PRACTICE AREA. THE GEAR WAS IN THIS CONFIGURATION FOR THE FIRST TWO LANDING ATTEMPTS, EITHER BECAUSE THE MOTOR BURNED OUT ON THE FIRST EXTENSION, OR FAILED AS A RESULT OF BEING COUNTER-LOADED BY CONTACT WITH THE RUNWAY ON THE FIRST EXTENSION.

THE CREW USED ONE FIRE BOTTLE IN FLIGHT AND DURING THE TAXI THEY USED THE ALTERNATE BOTTLE. AT THE GATE, A TECHNICIAN (MECHANIC) USED ANOTHER FIRE EXTINGUISHER TO SPRAY THE TURBINE/TAILPIPE AREA, AND AN AIRPORT FIRE TRUCK THEN SPRAYED THE INTAKE AND ENTIRE ENGINE AREA. ALL TURBINE COMPONENTS REMAINED WITHIN THE ENGINE CASE, HOWEVER THIS FAILURE WAS CONTAINED SINCE THERE WAS NO EVIDENCE OF THE FIRE SPREADING OUT OF THE ENGINE CASE. THERE WAS EVIDENCE OF MODERATE HEAT RADIATION DAMAGE SPREADING TO THE INTERNAL ENGINE COWLING, THRUST REVERSERS, PYLON FAIRING PANELS, ENGINE MOUNTS AND OTHER EXTERNAL ENGINE COMPONENTS. UNITED AIRLINES SFO ENGINEERING REVEALED THAT THIS V-2500 ENGINE, SERIAL NUMBER V10390 WAS A HIGH TIME ENGINE WITH 12,780 HOURS, 4380 CYCLES AND WAS THE ORIGINAL ENGINE THAT WAS DELIVERED WITH THE AIRCRAFT. DURING THIS INVESTIGATION IT WAS NOTED THAT THIS ENGINE HAD EXTENSIVE TROUBLESHOOTING FOR FLAMEOUT'S AT IDLE DURING THE PREVIOUS TWO DAYS AT ORD. SEVERAL COMPONENTS IN THE FUEL/BLEED VALVE SYSTEM WERE REPLACED, AIRCRAFT/ENGINES RUN NUMEROUS TIMES AT POWER, AND THE ORIGINAL PROBLEM FIXED. TROUBLESHOOTING OF THOSE PROBLEMS WAS DONE IN COORDINATION WITH SFO ENGINEERING AND DEFECTIVE COMPONENTS WERE CONFIRMED, UNITED AIRLINES ENGINEERING AND MAINTENANCE PERSONNEL WERE SATISFIED THAT THEY HAD FIXED THE PROBLEM BEFORE RELEASING THE AIRCRAFT AS SERVICEABLE BEFORE IT'S DEPARTURE ON FLIGHT 1676 ON MAY 29. THE AIRCRAFT WAS SUBSEQUENTLY TOWED TO THE MAINTENANCE HANGER WHERE THE ENGINE WAS REPLACED. IN ADDITION TO THE ENGINE, THE THRUST REVERSERS, REVERSER ACTUATORS, FIRE DETECTION LOOPS, FAN AIR VALVE, OVERPRESSURE VALVE, AND THE P2T2 SENSOR WERE REPLACED AND OTHER COMPONENTS REPAIRED, ALL DUE TO HEAT DAMAGE. THE PYLON STRUCTURE, ENGINE MOUNTS AND PYLON FAIRING PANELS WERE INSPECTED FOR HEAT DAMAGE AND WERE EITHER REPAIRED OR REPLACED AND IN SOME CASE TESTED OK. PRIOR TO DEPARTING PIE, THE DOOR WAS CHECKED VISUALLY, BUT NEITHER PILOT COULD RECALL IF THE SECURITY OF THE DOOR WAS CHECKED BEYOND A VISUAL CHECK OF THE HANDLE POSITION. THE AIRCRAFT MAINTENANCE RECORDS INDICATED REPEATED PROBLEMS WITH THE DOOR LATCHING MECHANISM, INCLUDING INSTANCES OF THE DOOR COMING OPEN IN FLIGHT. THE AIRCRAFT IS USED IN A TRAINING ENVIRONMENT AND, BY DESIGN, DOES NOT TOLERAE ROUGH HANDLING OR OUT-OF-SEQUENCE CLOSING/LATCHING PROCEDURES. THE BUILT-IN SAFETY MECHANISM CAN BE EASILY OVERRIDEN BY MANUALLY MOVING THE INSIDE DOOR HANDLE TO THE OPEN POSITION WITHOUT FIRST PULLING UP ON THE LATCH KNOB. THIS EFFECTIVELY CHANGES THE DOOR LATCH RIGGING. THE TOP DOOR PIN REQUIRED ADJUSTMENT AND THE LATCHING MECHANISM REQUIRED LUBRICATION SUBSEQUENT TO THE INCIDENT.

THE AIRCRAFT WAS DEPLANED NORMALLY AT THE GATE, ONE WOMAN ON BOARD WAS TREATED FOR A SEIZURE, HER CONDITION WAS UNRELATED TO THE LIGHTNING STRIKE. NO OTHER INJURIES WERE REPORTED. THE AIRCRAFT WAS THEN TAKEN TO A MAINTENANCE AREA FOR INSPECTION WHERE AMERICAN AIRLINES (AALA) MAINTENANCE PERSONNEL CONDUCTED A LIGHTING STRIKE INSPECTION. A DIME SIZE HOLE WAS NOTED AFT OF THE AIRCRAFT ENTRY DOOR DURING THIS INSPECTION. TWO INSPECTORS FROM THE O'HARE FSDO ARRIVED AT MDW ON JUNE 11, 2002 TO CONDUCT AN INCIDENT INVESTIGATION. THE INSPECTORS WERE ESCORTED TO THE AIRCRAFT, WHICH WAS PARKED ON A CLOSED TAXIWAY, BY THE AIRPORTS DEPARTMENT OF AVIATION PERSONNEL. WHEN AALA MECHANICS ARRIVED FROM ORD THEY TOWED THE AIRCRAFT TO TERMINAL GATE G-8 TO COMPLETE THE LIGHTINGSTRIKE INSPECTION WORK CARD AND PREPARE THE AIRCRAFT FOR A MAINTENANCE FERRY FLIGHT FROM MDW TO ORD FOR FURTHER EVALUATION OF THE LIGHTING STRIKE. MAINTENANCE FOUND THE AIRCRAFT TO BE IN A SAFE CONDITION FOR A MAINTENANCE FERRY FLIGHT AND PREPARED THE AIRCRAFT PER SPOTTING MESSAGE NUMBER 06054 AND ACTION TO BE TAKEN MESSAGE NUMBER 2CU531C74. THE MECHANICS APPLIED SPEED TAPE TO THE DAMAGED SKIN AREA TO PREVENT MOISTURE FROM ENTERING THE AIRCRAFT PER GPM 17-07 AND SECURED THE OUTFLOW VALVE OPEN PER MPM 21-18B. THE AIRCRAFT WAS SUBSEQUENTLY FERRIED TO ORD AND TOWED INTO THE MAINTENANCE HANGER WHERE THE DAMAGE WAS RE-INSPECTED AND REPAIRED. THE DAMAGED AREA HAD THE PAINT AND AIRCRAFT SKIN REMOVED, A DOUBLER WAS FABRICATED, ALODINED, PRIMED AND INSTALLED PER SRM 53-00-02-5R. THE AIRCRAFT SKIN WAS PRIMED AND A FINISHED COAT OF PAINT WAS APPLIED. IN ADDITION THE OUTFLOW VALVE WAS RE-INSTALLED AND OP'S CHECKED PER MM. THE AIRCRAFT WAS THEN RETURNED TO SERVICE. NOTE: INCIDENT PHOTOGRAPHS ARE IN THE CUSTODY OF THE REPORTING INSPECTOR.

THE PILOT ADDED THAT THE LANDING GEAR WAS HELD UP BY HYDRAULIC PRESSURE, AND THAT THE MOTOR WOULD OCCASIONALLY ACTIVATE FOR A FEW SECONDS, BUT THIS TIME, THE MOTOR CONTINUED TO RUN AND SOUNDED LIKE IT WAS NOT UNDER LOAD. ABOUT 1/2 MILE FROM THE RUNWAY, THE PILOT SELECTED FULL FLAPS, AND THE UNSAFE GEAR HORN SOUNDED. WHILE OVER THE RUNWAY, THE PILOT SECURED THE ENGINE, AND INITIATED A FLARE. THE AIRPLANE TOUCHED DOWN CLOSE TO STALL SPEED. ON THE GROUND, THE PILOT COULD FEEL THAT THE NOSE WHEEL WAS LOCKED DOWN, AND THAT THE PARTIALLY EXTENDED MAIN LANDING GEAR WAS DRAGGING ALONG SIDE THE AFT PORTION OF THE FUSELAGE. THE AIRPLANE DEPARTED THE RIGHT SIDE OF THE RUNWAY, AND CAME TO REST RIGHT WING LOW BETWEEN RUNWAYS 33 AND 29. THE PILOT RELEASED THE PASSENGER'S SEATBELT, AND THE PASSENGER "ROLLED" OUT OF THE AIRPLANE AND ONTO THE GROUND UNDER THE RIGHT WING. THE PILOT FINISHED SECURING THE AIRPLANE, AND THEN EXITED OUT THE SAME DOOR. ACCORDING TO A FEDERAL AVIATION ADMINISTRATION INSPECTOR THAT EXAMINED THE AIRPLANE AFTER THE ACCIDENT, HYDRAULIC FLUID WAS IDENTIFIED IN THE WHEEL WELL FOR THE NOSE GEAR, AND ALONG THE BOTTOM SIDE OF THE FUSELAGE. VISUAL METEOROLOGICAL CONDITIONS PREVAILED FOR THE SCHEDULED FLIGHT, AND AN INSTRUMENT FLIGHT RULES (IFR) FLIGHT PLAN WAS FILED AND ACTIVATED. THE FLIGHT WAS ORIGINATING AT THE TIME OF THE ACCIDENT. (-23) DURING TAKE OFF ROLL THE CREW NOTED AN APPARENT FLIGHT MANAGEMENT COMPUTER (FMC) MALFUNCTION AND A CORRESPONDING "INSTRUMENT ROLLBACK." IN THIS CONDITION THE FMC AIRSPEED DATA HAS AN INTERNAL COMPUTER DEFAULT OF "100 KTS." THIS FAILURE OF THE FMC COINCIDENTALLY OCCURRED AT THE TIME AND POINT THE AIRCRAFT WAS PASSING THROUGH "VI". THERE WAS A LACK OF SITUATIONAL AWARENESS AS INDICATED BY TWO ASPECTS, 1) THE CREW OBSERVED THE FAILURE BUT, DID                                                               NOT TRANSITION TO "RAW DATA" AVAILABLE ON THE STANDBY INDICATOR (PART OF FDEA CRM TRAINING) AND 2) THE FIRST OFFICE, THE NON-FLYING PILOT, APPEARS TO HAVE OVER-RELIED ON THE PLANNED "V2 REFERENCE DATA" AS OPPOSED TO VALIDATING WITH ACTUAL AIRSPEED. DURING THIS EVENT IT APPEARS HE MISTAKENLY MADE AN "EARLY" "VR" CALLOUT WHICH, WAS APPROXIMATELY 15 KNOTS TOO SLOW BY PERFORMANCE CALCULATIONS. THE CAPTAIN DID IN FACT "ROTATE" THE AIRCRAFT INTO A CLIMB ATTITUDE UPON THE CALLOUT. REALIZING THAT THIS CONFIGURATION AND PROFILE WERE UNACCEPTABLE HE THEN "REJECTED" THE TAKE-OFF BACK ONTO THE DEPARTURE RUNWAY. THE AIRCRAFT RECONTACTED THE RUNWAY IN A CLIMB ATTITUDE OF AT LEAST 12 DEGREES OF NOSE UP PITCH. THIS IS EVIDENCED BY THE "SUBSTANTIAL DAMAGE" NOTED IN THE AFT SECTION OF THE AIRCRAFT FUSELAGE, ONE STRUCTURAL FLOOR BEAM FORWARD OF THE AFT PRESSURE BULKHEAD. THIS DAMAGE CORRESPONDS DIRECTLY WITH A "TAIL STRIKE" SCENARIO WHICH IS NOTED HISTORICALLY WITH THIS MAKE AND MODEL OF AIRCRAFT.

20020613016519I	(-23) PRELIMINARY FINDINGS: LANDING AT SANTA MONICA, CA PILOT HAD THREE GREEN LIGHTS AND CLEARANCE TO LAND, UPON LANDING THE AIRCRAFT EXPERIENCED A PARTIAL NOSE GEAR COLLAPSE. AIRCRAFT TOUCHED DOWN ON MAIN WHEELS, PILOT LOWERED NOSE, FELT VIBRATION AND THOUGHT HE HAD A BLOWN NOSE TIRE. PILOT PULLED BACK ON THE YOKE AND BROUGHT THE NOSE UP AS LONG AS HE COULD HOLD IT, WHEN THE NOSE TOUCHED DOWN THE VIBRATION WAS GONE (NOSE GEAR THEN LOCKED DOWN). THE PILOT DID NOT REALIZE THAT HE HAD A PROP STRIKE UNTIL HE SHUT DOWN THE ENGINE. ATC SMO TOWER CONFIRMED THAT DURING THE LANDING THE AIRCRAFT APPEARED TO HAVE A PARTIAL GEAR COLLAPSE, PROP STRIKE AND TAXIED OFF THE RUNWAY UNDER IT'S OWN POWER. MAINTENANCE INSPECTION FOUND THAT THE NOSE LANDING GEAR MICRO SWITCH WAS OUT OF RIG ALLOWING A SAFE GEAR INDICATION, BUT SHUTTING OFF HYDRAULIC POWER AND NOT ALLOWING THE NOSE GEAR TO LOCK. MAINTENANCE ATTEMPTED TO RIG THE MICRO SWITCH AT SMO, BUT FOUND THAT THE SWITCH BRACKET WAS ADJUSTED TO THE END OF ITS TRAVEL AND THE MICRO SWITCH ACTUATOR SPRING HAD TO BE BENT TO PROPERLY RIG THE NOSE LANDING GEAR. THIS PROCEDURE IS CONTRARY TO THE PIPER AIRPLANE MAINTENANCE MANUAL 32-60-00 PAGE 32. THE AIRCRAFT WAS MANUFACTURED IN 2000, HAS LOW TIME AND MAINTENANCE RECORDS DO NOT INDICATE ANY PRIOR MAINTENANCE PERFORMED ON THE NOSE LANDING GEAR. THE PROPELLER WAS REPLACED, CRANKSHAFT RUNOUT CHECKED AND THE AIRCRAFT WAS ISSUED A SPECIAL FLIGHT PERMIT FROM SMO TO DVT (LANDING GEAR DOWN AND LOCKED) FOR MAINTENANCE AT CUTTER AVIATION INC., PHOENIX, AZ. FINAL REPORT TO FOLLOW PENDING TEARDOWN. (-23 AMENDMENT) FINAL FINDINGS: INVESTIGATION AT CUTTER AVIATION INC., PHOENIX, AZ. CONFIRMED THAT THE NOSE GEAR DOWN LIMIT SWITCH FOR NOSE DOWN LIGHT AND HYDRAULIC PUMP SHUT OFF WAS OUT OF ADJUSTMENT CAUSING THE PUMP TO SHUT OFF AND THE LIGHT TO INDICATE DOWN WITH THE NOSE GEAR NOT DOWN AND LOCKED. THE LIMIT SWITCH AND BRACKET ASSEMBLY WAS FOUND MOUNTED TOO FAR AWAY FROM THE DOWN LOCK HOOK AND MOUNTED IN THE IMPROPER HOLE. A NEW LIMIT SWITCH AND THE EXISTING BRACKET WERE MOUNTED ON THE FORWARD MOUNT HOLE, RIGGED PER THE MAINTENANCE MANUAL AND THE CORRECT CLEARANCE WAS OBTAINED. AS STATED IN THE PRELIMINARY FINDINGS A THOROUGH SEARCH OF ALL AIRCRAFT RECORDS WERE REVIEWED FOR HISTORY OF PRIOR WORK CONDUCTED ON THE LANDING GEAR SYSTEM AND NO                                                                REFERENCE WAS FOUND. IT IS IMPOSSIBLE TO STATE CAUSE OF DISCREPANCY, THIS COULD HAVE BEEN A MANUFACTURING ERROR THAT MANIFESTED OVER TIME WITH WEAR OR PERHAPS UNDOCUMENTED MAINTENANCE WAS CONDUCTED THAT THE OWNER/OPERATOR WAS UNAWARE OF.

WHEN N2571C MADE THE GO-AROUND, WITNESSES ON THE GROUND NOTICED THAT THE REAR ENGINE'S PROP WAS NOT TURNING. THE PILOT ALSO STATED HE FELT THAT THE AIRCRAFT WAS LOSING POWER. WHEN THE PILOT REENTERED BASE LEG TO FINAL, THE FRONT ENGINE FAILED. THE CESSNA PILOT OPERATING HANDBOOK HAS A NOTE IN SECTION II (FUEL SYSTEM) THAT STATES THE FUEL SELECTORS SHOULD BE ON "MAIN" FOR TAKE OFF AND LANDING AS WELL AS ALL NORMAL OPERATIONS. THE APPROVED CHECK LIST FOR THE CE-337 REQUIRES THE FUEL SELECTORS TO BE ON THE MAIN FUEL TANKS FOR TAKE OFF AND LANDING. THE TRAINING PROGRAM FOR THEAIRCRAFT REQUIRES TAKE OFF AND LANDINGS TO BE MADE WITH THE FUEL SELECTORS ON THE MAIN FUEL TANKS. DURING CHECK RIDES, ADHERENCE TO CHECK LISTS AND PROCEDURES ARE TESTED AND EACH LANDING OBSERVED MUST BE IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE MANUFACTURER RECOMMENDATIONS AND THE APPROVED CHECKLIST. THE MAIN AND AUXILIARY TANKS WERE TOPPED OFF AT THE BEGINNING OF THE DUTY DAY. THE AIRCRAFT HAD A TOTAL OF 128 GALLONS OF FUEL. THIS WOULD GIVE THE AIRCRAFT A MAXIMUM OF ALMOST TEN (10) HOURS ENDURANCE AT REDUCED POWER SETTINGS TO MOER THAN FIVE (5) HOURS AT HIGHER POWER SETTINGS. THE PILOT FLEW LESS THAN THREE HOURS WITH THE US FORREST SERVICE AT VARIOUS POWER SETTINGS BEFORE BEING RELEASED FROM THE SAN BERNARDINO INTERNATIONAL AIRPORT BASE FOR THE 15-MINUTE FLIGHT BACK TO BIG BEAR CITY AIRPORT. DEPENDING UPON THE POWER SETTINGS USED, THE AIRCRAFT WOULD HAVE HAD AS LITTLE AS 2 HOURS ENDURANCE AT MAX GROSS WEIGHT AND MAXIMUM POWER SETTINGS TO AS MUCH AS 6 HOURS OF FUEL REMAINING AT MINIMUM POWER SETTINGS. THE TWO AUXILIARY TANKS HOLD 19 GALLONS OF FUEL EACH WITH APPROXIMATELY 18 GALLONS OF FUEL USABLE IN FLIGHT. THE AUXILIARY TANKS PROVIDE BETWEEN .8 AND 1.5 HOURS OF FLIGHT TIME DEPENDING ON POWER SETTINGS SELECTED. ^PRIVACY DATA OMITTED^

HE MANEUVERED OVER THE RANCH, AND WAS IN A LEFT CLIMBING BANK ON HIS WAY BACK TO THE AIRPORT WHEN THE ENGINE QUIT. HE PUSHED THE ENGINE CONTROLS FORWARD, AND "SWITCHED THE FUEL SELECTOR TO THE AUX POSITION MOMENTARILY WITH STILL NO CHANGE NOTED." THE PILOT THEN MOVED THE FUEL SEL          ECTOR BACK TO THE RIGHT MAIN TANK, AND VERIFIED THAT THE CIRCUIT BREAKERS AND MAGNETOS WERE NORMAL. ALL EFFORTS TO RESTART THE ENGINE FAILED. THE PILOT MADE A FORCED LANDING IN A BEAN FIELD, SUBSEQUENTLY WRINKLING THE FUSELAGE, AND BENDING SEVERAL BULKHEADS AND THE LOWER CENTERLINE SPAR CARRY THROUGH MEMBERS. THE PILOT TOLD A FEDERAL AVIATION ADMINISTRATION (FAA) INSPECTOR THAT HE DEPARTED MONTROSE TO PRACTICE FLIGHT MANEUVERS. HE SAID HE WAS MANEUVERING THE AIRCRAFT BETWEEN 500 TO 1100 FEET ABOVE GROUND LEVEL WHILE PRACTICING GROUND MANEUVERS. THE PILOT SAID THE FUEL SELECTOR WAS ON THE LEFT MAIN TANK. THE ENGINE STARTED TO SPUTTER, AND HE SWITCHED THE SELECTOR TO THE RIGHT MAIN TANK, BUT DID NOT TURN ON THE BOOST PUMP. ALL ATTEMPTS TO RESTART THE ENGINE FAILED AND HE MADE A FORCED LANDING IN A BEAN FIELD. AN FAA INSPECTOR EXAMINED THE ACCIDENT AIRCRAFT ON JULY 6, 2002, AND FOUND THE LEFT MAIN FUEL TANK EMPTY, THE RIGHT MAIN TANK WAS APPROXIMATELY HALF FULL (ABOUT 11 GALLONS), AND THE AUXILIARY SELECTOR POSITION (TWO 10 GALLON TANKS FEED ONE POSITION) WITH APPROXIMATELY 15 GALLONS OF FUEL. CONTINUITY OF THE THROTTLE AND THE MIXTURE LINES WERE ESTABLISHED, AND NO ABNORMALITIES WEREFOUND IN ANY OF THE FUEL SYSTEM'S COMPONENTS. THE PILOT'S OPERATING HANDBOOK (POH) FOR THE AIRPLANE STATES THAT THE ENGINE AIR START PROCEDURE INCLUDES TURNING THE AUXILIARY FUEL PUMP ON "UNTIL POWER IS REGAINED, THEN OFF." A PUBLISHED TEMPORARY CHANGE TO THE POH STATES: THE ADDITION OF A PLACARD TO THE FUEL SELECTOR TO WARN OF THE NO-FLOW CONDITION THAT EXISTS BETWEEN THE FUEL SELECTOR DETENTS.

AT THIS TIME THE CAPTAIN PERFORMED AN EMERGENCY LEFT ENGINE SHUTDOWN, INSTRUCTED THE FIRST OFFICER TO FINISH THE SECURING CHECKLIST AND THE PASSENGERS TO STAY SEATED, AND EXITED THE AIRCRAFT TO LEND ASSISTANCE. HE STATED AT NO TIME WAS THE CAPTAIN'S ACCESS PORT OPEN. ACCORDING TO AN OFFICIAL WITH THE FAA, THE RAMP AGENT HAD JUST PLACED CHOCKS AGAINST THE NOSE TIRES OF THE ARRIVING FLIGHT, AND AS SHE APPROACHED THE CAPTAIN'S ACCESS PORT TO DELIVER FLIGHT DOCUMENTS TO THE CREW, THE PORT HAD NOT BEEN OPENED. SHE THEN STUFFED THE PAPERS INTO HER BREAST POCKET AND READJUSTED THE NOSE GEAR CHOCKS. AS SHE APPROACHED THE CAPTAIN'S ACCESS PORT FOR THE SECOND TIME, THE DOCUMENTS BLEW OUT OF HER BREAST POCKET. AS SHE SCURRIED TO RETRIEVE THEM, HER RIGHT HAND CONTACTED THE ENGINE NUMBER ONE ROTATING PROPELLER. THE PROPELLER WAS FEATHERED AND WINDING DOWN WHEN THE ACCIDENT OCCURRED. THE RAMP AGENT'S RIGHT THUMB AND TWO ADJACENT FINGERS WERE SEVERED. ACCORDING TO THE CHIEF PILOT OF MESABA AIRLINES, THE RAMP AGENT WAS AN EMPLOYEE OF PINNACLE AIRLINES WHO CONTRACTS WITH MESABA TO CONDUCT GROUND HANDLING OF AIRCRAFT AT THE TUPELO AIRPORT. THE MESABA GROUND HANDLING MANUAL STATES THAT ANY PART OF THE RAMP AFT OF THE NOSE GEAR OF THE SAAB 340 IS A PROHIBITED ZONE AND IS NOT TO BE OCCUPIED UNTIL PROPELLERS HAVE STOPPED ROTATING. THE TUPELO STATION MANAGER FOR PINNACLE AIRLINES CONFIRMED THAT THE TRAINING GIVEN TO THEIR RAMP AGENTS STATES THAT NO PART OF THE RAMP AFT OF THE SAAB'SFRONT LOADING DOOR SHOULD BE OCCUPIED UNTIL PROPELLERS HAVE STOPPED. THE ACCIDENT RAMP AGENT HAD RECEIVED THE TRAINING. HE STATED FURTHER THAT THE ACCIDENT HAPPENED, PRIMARILY, DUE TO IMPULSE REACTION WHEN THE DISPATCH PAPERS BLEW OUT OF THE AGENT'S BREAST POCKET.

SHE WAS INSTRUCTED TO PROCEED TO PARKING AT THE EAST RAMP, VIA TAXIWAYS BRAVO, ECHO, AND ROMEO. THE PA-31 PILOT STATED THAT WHILE TAXIING SLOWLY ON TAXIWAY ROMEO, AND WHILE MAKING A LEFT TURN ONTO TAXIWAY CHARLIE, SHE HEARD ONE OF HER PASSENGERS SEATED IN REAR END AND ON THE RIGHT SIDE OF THE AIRPLANE YELL SOMETHING. SUBSEQUENTLY, THE RIGHT PROPELLER OF THE TAXIING PA-31 COLLIDED WITH THE AFT PORTION OF THE CESSNA 172'S LEFT WING AND AILERON. THE PA-31 SUSTAINED NO DAMAGE DURING THE COLLISION. BOTH PILOTS COMMENTED THAT CONSTRUCTION ACTIVITY IN THE AREA COMPLICATED TAXI PROCEDURES. BOTH PILOTS ACKNOWLEDGED THAT THE AREA IN WHICH THE COLLISION TOOK PLACE WAS CONSIDERED "UNCONTROLLED" BY FAIRBANKS ATCT GROUND CONTROL. THE AIRCRAFT CONTINUED TO ROLL LEFT 20 TO 25 DEGREES BEFORE IT WAS MANUALLY CORRECTED USING THE AILERON CONTROL WHEEL. THE AIRCRAFT RECOVERED AND NO OTHER CONTROL PROBLEMS WERE NOTED. THE SPEED BRAKE HANDLE WAS DOWN, THERE WERE NO TRIM INPUTS PRIOR TO THE EVENT AND NO UNUSUAL WHEEL OR RUDDER FORCES WERE NOTED. THE CREW WENT THROUGH THE ABNORMAL PROCEDURE, DISCONNECTED THE YAW DAMPER, BUT DID NOT SHUT OFF HYDRAULICS DUE TO THIS INCIDENT NOT BEING A "RUDDER HARDOVER." UNITED AIRLINES ORD MAINTENANCE, IN COORDINATION WITH LINE ENGINEERING AND FLIGHT SAFETY TROUBLESHOT AND CONDUCTED A THOROUGH AND EXHAUSTIVE CHECK AND INSPECTION OF ALL RELATED FLIGHT CONTROL SYSTEMS AND COMPONENTS. THE PRIMARY GUIDANCE FOR THIS TROUBLESHOOTING WAS BOEINGS SERVICE LETTER NUMBER 737-SL-27-110-A, DATED 14 SEPTEMBER 2001. SUBJECT: "UNEXPECTED ROLL AND YAW EVENT TROUBLESHOOTING." AS PART OF THE TROUBLESHOOTING PROCEDURES AND RESULTING INSPECTION AND CHECKS OF THE SYSTEMS AND COMPONENTS, THE FOLLOWING COMPONENTS WERE REMOVED AND REPLACED PER THE MAINTENANCE MANUAL: FLIGHT DATA RECORDER, MAIN RUDDER POWER CONTROL UNIT. STANDBY RUDDER ACTUATOR AND THE YAW DAMP COUPLER. IN ADDITION, DURING THE RUDDER ACTUATION CHECK, A BINDING PULLEY WAS NOTED IN THE FORWARD CARGO PIT CEILING AND IT WAS REPLACED. ALL RELATED HYDRAULIC FILTERS WERE REPLACED AND FLUID SAMPLES FROM THE A AND B HYDRAULIC SYSTEMS WERE TAKEN FOR ANALYSIS. DURING THE SYSTEM CHECK OUTS AND TROUBLESHOOTING OF THE RUDDERS (PCU) MAIN POWER CONTROL UNIT, IT WAS NOTED THAT IT DID NOT HAVE A CONSISTENT NEUTRAL. AFTER "SHAKE-OUT" THE RUDDER WOULD RETURN TO A DIFFERENTNEUTRAL EACH TIME WITH A TENDENCY TOWARD THE RIGHT 3/4 INCH. IN ADDITION DURING THIS CHECK OUT THE STAND BY RUDDER ACTUATOR WAS FOUND TO HAVE AN INCONSISTENT FREE-PLAY AND A NEUTRAL 3/4 INCH TO THE LEFT. BOTH OF THESE UNITS WERE SUBSEQUENTLY REPLACED. IN CONCLUSION, THE RUDDER POWER CONTROL UNIT, YAW DAMP COUPLER, AND THE STANDBY RUDDER ACTUATOR WERE REPLACED DUE TO DISCREPANCIES AND AS A PRECAUTION AS RECOMMENDED BY UNITED AIRLINES FLIGHT SAFETY AND ENGINEERING. NO DEFINITE CONCLUSIONS HAVE YET BEEN REACHED AS TO THE SPECIFIC CAUSE FOR THIS UNCOMMANDED ROLL. ALL OF THE DATA HAS NOT BEEN EVALUATED YET, SUCH AS THE RADAR DATA, VOICE RECORDER, OR QAR (QUICK ACCESS RECORDER). THE REMOVED COMPONENTS HAVE BEEN SENT TO UNITED AIRLINES SHOPS FOR TEAR DOWN AND EVALUATION, A FINAL REPORT WITH A CONCLUSION WILL BE PROVIDED BY UNITED AIRLINES AT A LATER DATE. THE SUBJECT AIRCRAFT, N307UA, B737-322 WAS RELEASED FOR SERVICE ON AUGUST 19, 2002 AND AT THE TIME OF THIS REPORT HAD EXPERIENCED NO DIFFICULTIES.

THE FLIGHT ORIGINATED AT DELTA AT 0953, AND WAS EN ROUTE TO ALBANY WITH UNKNOWN INTERMEDIATE STOPS. PRELIMINARY INFORMATION INDICATES THE AIRPLANE HAD UNDERGONE AN ANNUAL INSPECTION ON AUGUST 22, 2002, ITS SALE HAD RECENTLY BEEN CONSUMMATED, AND THE PILOT HAD VOLUNTEERED TO FERRY THE AIRPLANE TO ALBANY. THE AIRPLANE HAD BEEN FUELED TO CAPACITY (60 GALLONS). THE PILOT, CARRYING A FLIGHT BAG AND AN OVERNIGHT KIT, BOARDED THE AIRPLANE AND TAXIED TO THE END OF RUNWAY 03, WHERE HE PERFORMED PRETAKEOFF CHECKS. THE AIRPORT MANAGER SAID THE MAGNETO CHECKS SOUNDED NORMAL, BUT AS SOON AS THE PILOT ADDED TAKEOFF POWER, HE "KNEW SOMETHING WAS WRONG." HE SAID THE ENGINE DID NOT SOUND LIKE IT WAS PRODUCING FULL POWER AND THE AIRPLANE WAS NOT ACCELERATING. THE AIRPORT MANAGER SAID THE AIRPLANE LIFTED OFF NEAR THE END OF THE 5,600-FOOT RUNWAY (1.5% UPHILL GRADE), FLEW IN GROUND EFFECT AND BARELY CLEARED A BARBED WIRE PERIMETER FENCE, THEN DISAPPEARED INTO A VALLEY. SHORTLY THEREAFTER HE OBSERVED SMOKE. WITNESSES ON A GOLF COURSE NEAR THE ACCIDENT SITE SAID THE ENGINE WAS "SPUTTERING." EXAMINATION OF THE AIRPLANE AND ACCIDENT SITE INDICATES THE AIRPLANE STRUCK THE GROUND IN A RIGHT WING AND NOSE LOW ATTITUDE. BOTH WING FUEL TANKS WERE BREACHED. THE FLAPS ON THE FIXED GEAR AIRPLANE WERE RETRACTED. THERE WAS LITTLE EVIDENCE OF PROPELLER ROTATION. CONTINUITY WAS ESTABLISHED FROM THE VARIOUS CONTROL SURFACES TO THE COCKPIT AREA. ACCORDING TO THE PILOT, ON LABOR DAY, HE DEPARTED BROWNSVILLE, TEXAS, FOR SCOTTSDALE WITH A PLANNED REFUELING STOP AT PECOS, TEXAS. ABOUT 30 MINUTES PAST DEL RIO, WHILE IN CRUISE FLIGHT AT 10,500 FEET MSL, "THE ENGINE QUIT WITHOUT WARNING." HE IMMEDIATELY MADE A TURN BACK TO DEL RIO, AND THEN SWITCHED FUEL TANKS, CYCLED THE BOOST PUMP, MIXTURE CONTROL, ETC., AND SET UP A BEST GLIDE SPEED OF 105 KNOTS. "AFTER SOME FIDDLING [HE] DETERMINED THAT THE ENGINE WOULD PRODUCE SOME POWER USING THE AUX PUMP ON THE HIGH BOOST POSITION RESULTING IN A VERY LOW POWER SETTING." HE CONTINUED TO THE DEL RIO INTERNATIONAL AIRPORT AND LANDED THE AIRPLANE WITHOUT FURTHER INCIDENT. AFTER CONVERSATIONS WITH A LOCAL AIRCRAFT MECHANIC, IT WAS DETERMINED THAT THE LIKELY PROBLEM WAS THE FAILURE OF THE ENGINE DRIVEN FUEL PUMP. THE MECHANIC REMOVED THE FUEL PUMP, REBUILT IT, AND THE SAME FUEL PUMP WAS REINSTALLED ON THE ENGINE. ON THE DAY OF THE ACCIDENT, THE PILOT COMPLETED A PREFLIGHT DURING WHICH THE FUEL WAS SUMPED. AFTER THE FUEL TANKS WERE TOPPED OFF, THE PILOT STARTED THE ENGINE. HE STATED "THAT THE START-UP WAS A BIT DIFFERENT FROM WHAT [HE] WAS USED TO, IN THAT GENERALLY AFTER THE ENGINE STARTS, IF THERE IS ANY STUMBLING OR ROUGHNESS, A QUICK PULSE OF THE AUX PUMP ON LOW USUALLY CLEARS ANY VAPOR REMAINING IN THE FUEL LINE. HOWEVER, WHEN [HE] PULSED THE AUX PUMP ON LOW THIS TIME, THE ENGINE ALMOST DIED. OPERATING THE ENGINE AT ABOUT 1500 RPM FOR 5-10 SECONDS SEEM TO CLEARED IT UP, AND IT SEEMED SMOOTH AND OPERATING IN A NORMAL MANNER." THE PILOT REPORTED THAT HE TAXIED THE AIRPLANE TO RUNWAY 13 AND COMPLETED A "NORMAL" RUN UP. AFTER PERFORMING THE BEFORE TAKEOFF CHECKS, HE TAXIED THE AIRPLANE ONTO THE RUNWAY, HELD THE BRAKES, AND APPLIED FULL THROTTLE. "IT TOOK A FEW SECONDS FOR THE ENGINE TO REACH 32.5" MP (TAKEOFF POWER) AS IT USUALLY DOES, AND [HE] OBSERVED THE FUEL FLOW TO BE NOT AT, BUT VERY CLOSE TO THE RED LINE PRESSURE (WHERE IT IS SUPPOSED TO BE). THE FUEL FLOW WAS IN ROUGHLY THE SAME POSITION ON THE GAUGE AS IT HAS BEEN IN THIS AIRPLANE FOR MANY YEARS, SO [HE] DEEMED THAT IT WAS ACCEPTABLE." AT FULL POWER, HE HELD THE BRAKES FOR 30-40 SECONDS, "CHECKED THE CHT AND EGTS AND FUEL FLOW, EVERYTHING WAS WITHIN NORMAL LIMITS" SO HE STARTED THE TAKEOFF ROLL. ABOUT 50 FEET AGL, THE PILOT RETRACTED THE LANDING GEAR AND ESTABLISHED AN 90 KNOT CLIMB. "JUST AS THE GEAR HAD CYCLED UP, ABOUT 100 FEET AGL, THE ENGINE QUIT COMPLETELY." HE SWITCHED FUEL TANKS AND TURNED ON THE BOOST PUMP, BUT IT HAD NO EFFECT. HE SELECTED A FIELD TO LAND IN AND EXTENDED THE LANDING GEAR AND FLAPS. THE NOSE LANDING GEAR "CLIPPED THE AIRPORT FENCE, AND [HE] MADE A GENTLE LEFT TURN (ABOUT 20 DEGREES) TO AIM FOR THE LONGEST PART OF THE FIELD." THE MAIN LANDING GEAR TOUCHED DOWN AND HE HELD THE NOSE UP AS LONG AS POSSIBLE, BUT WHEN IT CAME DOWN, IT STARTED SKIDDING ALONG THE GROUND. THE AIRPLANE CAME TO A STOP UPRIGHT IN A DITCH. REASON "O" RING POPPED OUT WAS WORN ACTUATOR PISTON, ALLOWING FOR EXCESSIVE CLEARANCE BETWEEN PISTGON, AND CYLINDER. DOWN LOCK ACTUATOR OVERHUAL MANUAL WAS CHECKED FOR TOLERANCE LIMITS. PISTON MET LIMITS OUTLINED IN OVERHAUL MANUAL. TO PREVENT THIS FROM HAPPENING AGAIN, FLYING BOAT HAS INITIATED TWO STEPS. STEP ONE IS TO TAKE ALL AVAILABLE BLUE PRINTS FOR ACTUATOR, AND HAVE THEIR FAA DESIGNATED ENGINEER REPRESENTATIVE INITIATE STEPS FOR FLYING BOAT TO MANUFACTURE NEW ACTUATORS. STEP TWO IS EXAMINE ALL SPARE ACTUATORS FOR TOLERANCE LIMITS, AND REJECT UNITS THAT AREA CLOSE TO EXISTING LIMITS. AS NEW ACTUATORS BECOME AVAILABLE, THEY WILL REPLACE EXISTING UNITS INSTALLED ON AIRCRAFT.

THE OPERATIONS MANAGER ADDITIONALLY STATED THAT HE DID NOT OBSERVE THE AIRPLANE FLY AT ANY TIME THE AIRPLANE WAS AT THE AIRPORT. A MECHANIC, WHO WORKED AT I73, STATED THAT HE HAD HELPED THE PILOT PREPARE THE AIRPLANE FOR THE FLIGHT, BY DRAINING ABOUT 2-1/2 GALLONS OF WATER FROM THE CENTER SUMP DRAIN LOCATED UNDER THE MAIN FUSELAGE, PRIOR TO THE AIRPLANE BEING FUELED. A WITNESS, WHO WAS A PILOT, OBSERVED THE ACCIDENT AIRPLANE AS IT WAS DEPARTING FROM RUNWAY 26, A 3,500-FOOT LONG ASPHALT RUNWAY. HE STATED THAT THE AIRPLANE'S ENGINES SOUNDED LIKE THEY WERE RUNNING GOOD, BUT DID NOT SOUND LIKE THEY WERE DEVELOPING FULL POWER. AS THE AIRPLANE CONTINUED DOWN THE RUNWAY, IT APPEARED TO BE TRAVELING VERY SLOWLY, AND NOT GAINING SUFFICIENT SPEED FOR TAKEOFF. THE AIRPLANE LIFTED ABRUPTLY INTO THE AIR ABOUT 3/4 OF THE WAY DOWN THE RUNWAY, AND THE LANDING GEAR WAS RETRACTED. THE AIRPLANE SETTLED TOWARDS THE GROUND, CLEARING THE LEVEE LOCATED AT THE DEPARTURE END OF THE RUNWAY BY A FEW FEET. THE AIRPLANE THEN BEGAN A CLIMB AGAIN, REACHING A HEIGHT OF ABOUT 120 FEET, AND PROCEEDED STRAIGHT OUT FROM THE AIRPORT. ABOUT 30 SECONDS LATER, THE AIRPLANE BANKED GENTLY TO THE LEFT, WHERE A FAINT PUFF OF BLACK SMOKE WAS OBSERVED COMING FROM AN ENGINE. AS THE BANK CONTINUED, THE AIRPLANE DESCENDED INTO A NEAR VERTICAL DIVE. THE WITNESS OBSERVED THE TOP PORTION OF THE AIRPLANE AS IT WAS IN THE VERTICAL DIVE, BEFORE IT DESCENDED OUT OF SIGHT. THE WITNESS ALSO RECALLED THAT THE PROPELLERS SOUNDED LIKE THEY WERE SYNCHED, AND WERE NOT MAKING ANY ABNORMAL NOISES. THE AIRPLANE CAME TO REST UPRIGHT IN A RESIDENTIAL AREA ABOUT 1 MILE SOUTHWEST OF I73, AND A POST CRASH FIRE ENSUED. THE POST CRASH FIRE ALSO DAMAGED TWO RESIDENTIAL HOMES AND A PARKED CAR. THE ACCIDENT SITE WAS DISTURBED PRIOR TO THE ARRIVAL OF SAFETY BOARD PERSONNEL DUE TO EMERGENCY RESCUE PROCEDURES. IN ADDITION, THE AREA HAD BEEN DOUSED WITH WATER AND FIREFIGHTING AGENTS TO CONTAIN THE POST CRASH FIRE. THE FIRST IMPACT AREA WAS LOCATED IN THE FRONT YARD OF ONE OF THE RESIDENTIAL HOMES. IT CONSISTED OF TWO CRATERS, CONTAINING THE LEFT AND RIGHT PROPELLER ASSEMBLIES, AND TWO 5-INCH WIDE, 3-INCH DEEP IMPRESSIONS IN THE GROUND. THE IMPRESSIONS WERE ABOUT 15 FEET IN LENGTH, AND WERE ORIENTATED ABOUT A HEADING OF 290 DEGREES MAGNETIC. ABOUT 24 FEET BEYOND THE EDGE OF THE LEFT IMPRESSION WAS A 3-FOOT SECTION OF THE LEFT OUTBOARD WINGTIP. ABOUT 75 FEET BEYOND THE RIGHT IMPRESSION WAS A 3-FOOT SECTION OF THE RIGHT OUTBOARD WINGTIP, WHICH CAME TO REST IN A ROAD. THE MAIN WRECKAGE CAME TO REST ON A 245-DEGREE MAGNETIC HEADING, ON TOP OF A CONCRETE SIDEWALK, ABOUT 32 FEET BEHIND THE FIRST IMPACT POINT. THE LOWER CRANKCASE WAS INSPECTED THROUGH THE INTAKE PORTS AND THE CONNECTING ROD FIT TO CRANKSHAFT WAS CHECKED AND DETERMINED TO BE SATISFACTORY. THE EXHAUST SYSTEM WAS REMOVED AND THE PISTONS AND COMBUSTION CHAMBERS WERE INSPECTED AND FOUND FREE FROM DAMAGE. HONE MARKS WERE VISIBLE INSIDE BOTH COMBUSTION CHAMBERS, PISTON RINGS WERE FREE WITHIN THE RING GROOVES AND THERE WAS NO CARBON BUILDUP ON THE PISTON DOMES. THE ENGINE WAS REMOVED FROM THE AIRFRAME AND TAKEN TO LEADING EDGE AIRFOILS (LEAF) AND PLACED ON AN ENGINE TEST FIXTURE. THE ENGINE STARTED WITHOUT EFFORT AND PRODUCED POWER AS DESIGNED. NO ABNORMALITIES WERE NOTED.

THE AIRCRAFT STRUCK THE GROUND WITH A HIGH VERTICAL MOMENT COLLAPSING THE MAIN LANDING GEAR. THE RIGHT WINGTIP, CATCHING THE HIGH GRASS, SPUN THE AIRCRAFT SO THAT IT SLID TAIL FIRST IN THE DRAINAGE DITCH UNTIL THE AIRCRAFT CAME TO REST. INSPECTION OF THE AIRCRAFT IN THE OWNER'S HANGAR REVEALED THAT THE PROPELLER WAS NOT TURNING WHEN THE AIRCRAFT STRUCK THE GROUND. THE LOWER COWLING HAD COME IN CONTACT WITH THE GROUND AND WAS SHEARED FROM THE AIRFRAME. THE LOWER PORTION OF THE CARBURETOR (BOWL) WAS SHEARED FROM IT'S MATING HALF AT INITIAL IMPACT. THE UPPER HALF OF THE CARBURETOR (VENTURI/THROTTLE BUTTERFLY) REMAINED ATTACHED TO THE ENGINE AND WAS FOUND OPERATING NORMALLY. THERE WAS AMPLE FUEL IN THE FUEL TANKS, THE ELECTRIC FUEL PUMP AND THE MECHANICAL ENGINE DRIVEN PUMP WERE TESTED AND OPERATED NORMALLY. THERE WAS AMPLE COMPRESSION ON ALL CYLINDERS. THE LEFT MAGNETO WAS OPERATING NORMALLY AND FIRED ON ALL CYLINDERS. THE RIGHT IGNITION SYSTEM IS ELECTRONIC AND WAS NOT TESTED. IT WAS NOT POSSIBLE TO RUN THE ENGINE DURING THE INITIAL INSPECTION. AN ENGINE RUN WILL BE PERFORMED WHEN IT IS POSSIBLE TO DO SO.

20021027038551A	(-23) ON OCTOBER 27, 2002, ABOUT 1330 EASTERN STANDARD TIME, A CESSNA 172M, N9840V, REGISTERED TO POWER SYSTEMS LTD, INC., AND OPERATED BY AMERICAN FLYING CLUB INC. AS A TITLE 14 CFR PART 91 INSTRUCTIONAL FLIGHT, AND A CESSNA 172N, N6101F, REGISTERED TO A PRIVATE INDIVIDUAL, AND OPERATED BY AIRBORNE SYSTEMS INC., AS A TITLE 14 CFR PART 91 INSTRUCTIONAL FLIGHT, COLLIDED WHILE IN CRUISE FLIGHT IN CORAL SPRINGS, FLORIDA. VISUAL METEOROLOGICAL CONDITIONS PREVAILED, AND NO FLIGHT PLANS WERE FILED FOR EITHER FLIGHT. N9840V WAS DESTROYED AND THE PRIVATE-RATED DUAL STUDENT AND THE COMMERCIAL-RATED FLIGHT INSTRUCTOR IN N9840V RECEIVED FATAL INJURIES. N6101F INCURRED SUBSTANTIAL DAMAGE, AND THE PRIVATE-RATED DUAL STUDENT AND THE COMMERCIAL-RATED FLIGHT INSTRUCTOR IN N6101F RECEIVED NO INJURIES. BOTH FLIGHTS ORIGINATED FROM FORT LAUDERDALE EXECUTIVE AIRPORT, FORT LAUDERDALE, FLORIDA, THE SAME DAY, ABOUT 1245. ACCORDING TO THE DUAL STUDENT IN N6101F, HE AND HIS FLIGHT INSTRUCTOR HAD BEEN FLYING IN THE PRACTICE AREA WEST OF FORT LAUDERDALE, FLORIDA, AND THEY HAD PERFORMED "8'S ON PYLONS AND LAZY 8'S", AS PART OF THE COMMERCIAL MANEUVERS TRAINING IN PURSUIT OF AN FAA COMMERCIAL PILOT CERTIFICATE. THE STUDENT SAID HE WAS THE PILOT FLYING N6101F, AND THEY WERE PROCEEDING SOUTHEAST BOUND AT AN ALTITUDE OF 2,000 FEET, ON A 120-DEGREE MAGNETIC BEARING TO THE "WSBR 740 AM RADIO TOWER. AS THEY NEARED THE "740 TOWER", HE SAID THEY WERE RECEIVING NEEDLE FLUCTUATIONS ON N6101F'S ADF INDICATOR, INDICATIVE OF THEM BEING VERY CLOSE TO THE TOWER, WHEN ALL OF A SUDDEN, AN AIRPLANE APPEARED VERY CLOSE, IN THE RIGHT CORNER OF THEIR AIRPLANE'S WINDSHIELD, HAVING COME FROM BEHIND THE BLIND SPOT CREATED BY THEIR AIRPLANE'S RIGHT WING. HE SAID IF LOOKED AS IF THE PILOT OF THE OTHER AIRPLANE SAW THEM ABOUT THE SAME TIME, AND THINKS THAT BOTH HE AND THE OTHER PILOT IMMEDIATELY INITIATED RIGHT TURNS IN AN ATTEMPT TO AVOID THE OTHER. THE STUDENT FURTHER STATED THAT AS HE INITIATED THE RIGHT TURN, THE OTHER AIRPLANE APPEARED TO EFFECTIVELY TRAVEL ACROSS HIS AIRPLANE'S WIND SHIELD FROM RIGHT TO LEFT, REMAINING JUST ABOVE THE GLARE SHIELD COVERING HIS AIRPLANE'S INSTRUMENT PANEL. HE SAID HE THEN FELT THE IMPACT OF HIS AIRPLANE'S LEFT WING COLLIDING WITH SOME PORTION OF THE OTHER AIRPLANE, AND HIS AIRPLANE "TUMBLED", AND ENTERED A SPIN TO THE LEFT. DURING THE SPIN, HE SAID HE SAW ANOTHER AIRPLANE ABOUT 250 TO 300 FEET BELOW HIM AND IT APPEARED TO BE INVERTED. THE INSTRUCTOR TOOK CONTROL OF N6101F FROM THE STUDENT, MADE EMERGENCY COMMUNICATION TRANSMISSIONS TO ADVISE OTHERS OF THE SITUATION, AND AFFECTED AN EMERGENCY LANDING TO A DIRT ROAD PARALLELING THE THEN BUSY SAWGRASS EXPRESSWAY. THE OTHER AIRPLANE IN THE COLLISION, N9840V IMPACTED A DIRT ROAD IN A ROCK QUARRY IN THE VICINITY OF THE LOXAHATCHEE NATIONAL WILDLIFE REFUGE, IN UNINCORPORATED PALM BEACH COUNTY, AND WAS DESTROYED ON IMPACT.

NOVEMBER 10, 2002 INSPECTORS ROSSI, MAURO AND GILLESSEN INSPECTED THE DEBRIS HELD AT THE EAST HAMPTON POLICE HEADQUARTERS. IT WAS CONFIRMED THAT THE AIRCRAFT WAS N911XW BY DATA PLATES FOUND ON DIFFERENT PIECES OF THE AIRCRAFT. A BACK PACK AND SMALL BAG WAS WASHED TO SHORE CONTAINING PERSONAL ARTIFACTS WHICH SEEMED TO IDENTIFY THE PILOT AS WILLIAM M. SMITHERS. IT WAS CONFIRMED THAT WILLIAM SMITHERS WAS THE PIC OF N911XW BY PETER BORNEMAN. NOVEMBER 12, 200W INSPECTORS ROSSI AND GILLISSEN INTERVIEWED MR. PETER BORNEMAN. HE INFORMED US THAT THE AIRCRAFT WAS NOT INSURED, THE PAINT WASNOT COMPLETE YET, THE INTERIOR WAS NOT COMPLETE YET, AND THEY HAD NOT RECEIVED OPERATING LIMITATIONS OR AN AIRWORTHINESS CERTIFICATE. HE STATED THAT THIS FLIGHT MAY HAVE BEEN MR. SMITHERS THIRD FLIGHT IN THE AIRCRAFT. HE SAID THAT MR. SMITHERS WIFE WAS CALLING HIM ALL MORNING, THAT HE SHOULD HAVE BEEN HOME BY THEN. MR. BORNEMAN THEN CONTACTED THE SUFFOLK POLICE DEPARTMENT AND ISP TOWER AND REPORTED THE OVERDUE AIRCRAFT. NOVEMBER 13, 2002 INSPECTOR ROSSI RECEIVED A CALL FROM THE US COAST GUARD TO REPORT THAT A TRAWLER BOAT, THE MISS SANDY, HAD PULLED UP THE TRANSMISSION, ROTOR BLADES AND A HUB AT COORDINATES 405319N AND 07216.10W. NOVEMBER 15, 2002 INSPECTOR GILLISSEN TOOK PHOTOS OF THE WRECKAGE THAT WAS RETRIEVED BY THE MISS SANDY, AND INSPECTED WHAT HE COULD. NOVEMBER 19, 2002 MP3 FILES OF MR. SMITHERS TALKING TO ISP GROUND AND ISP TOWER WERE RECEIVED AT THE FARMINGDALE FSDO. THERE WAS NOTHING OUT OF THE ORDINARY ON THE AUDIO. THE RADAR PLOT WAS RECEIVED AT THE FSDO ON NOVEMBER 21, 2002. IT REVEALED THAT N911XW WENT OFF THE RADAR AT 0422 UTC WITH AN ALTITUDE OF 800 FEET AND AN AIRSPEED OF 153 KNOTS. DURING THE LAST MINUTE, N911XW WAS DESCENDING AT 1100 FEET PER MINUTE. NOVEMBER 21, 2002 ALL EVIDENCE OF FACTS AND CIRCUMSTANCES WERE COLLECTED AND DOCUMENTED IN THE ACCIDENT FILE FOR THIS CASE. IT WAS FOUND THAT MR. SMITHERS WAS FLYING N911XW WITHOUT A VALID AIRWORTHINESS CERTIFICATE. THE CAUSE OF THE ACCIDENT WILL BE DETERMINED BY THE NTSB. BRIAN RAYNER IS THE NTSB IIC FOR THIS CASE. THE PILOT STATED, "THE APPROACH NEEDED TO LAND IS STEEPER THAN MOST PUBLIC AIRPORTS DUE TO THE TREES." THE AIRCRAFT SUSTAINED CRUSHING OF THE RIGHT WING OUTER PANEL AND SPAR EXTENSION ABOUT 3 TO 4 FEET INBOARD OF THE RIGHT WINGTIP. NO CONVECTIVE ACTIVITY WAS REPORTED AT EITHER MCCOMB OR HATTIESBURG'S CLOSEST (TO THE TIME OF THE ACCIDENT) REPORTED WEATHER REPORTS THAT MIGHT HAVE CAUSED WIND GUST-FRONT ACTIVITY. THE WINDS REPORTED BY MCCOMB, (29 MILES WEST OF THE AIRSTRIP) WERE FROM 220 DEGREES AT 12 KNOTS, GUSTING TO 23 KNOTS. THE WINDS REPORTED BY HATTIESBURG, (31 MILES EAST-NORTHEAST OF THE AIRSTRIP) WERE FROM 210 DEGREES AT 12 KNOTS, GUSTING TO 22 KNOTS.

A LATER EXAMINATION OF THE NOSE LANDING GEAR AND SUPPORT ASSEMBLY WAS CONDUCTED AND NO AIRCRAFT STRUCTURAL OR LANDING GEAR SUPPORT ASSEMBLY DAMAGE WAS NOTED OTHER THAN TO THE WHEEL AND TIRE ASSEMBLIES AND SHOCK ABSORBER AXLE. THE AIRCRAFT NOSE WAS JACKED UP ON THE RUNWAY ENOUGH TO REMOVE WHAT WAS LEFT OF THE RIGHT WHEEL AND TIRE ASSEMBLY AND A NEW WHEEL WAS INSTALLED. THE LEFT WHEEL HAD WORN DOWN INTO THE AXLE AND NEW WHEEL COULD NOT BE IMMEDIATELY INSTALLED WHILE THE AIRCRAFT WAS STILL ON THE RUNWAY. THE AIRCRAFT WAS THOROUGHLY INSPECTED BY MAINTENANCE AND ENGINEERING FOR OTHER DAMAGE OF WHICH LITTLE WAS NOTED OTHER THAN TO THE NOSE LANDING GEAR. THE SHOCK ABSORBER AND AXLE ASSEMBLY WAS REMOVED FOR INSPECTION AND PRELIMINARY EVIDENCE INDICATES THAT THE SHOCK ABSORBER ANTI-ROTATION LUGS AND THE SHOCK STRUT UPPER SUPPORT FITTING WERE NOT PROPERLY ALIGNED DURING PREVIOUS MAINTENANCE TO THE LANDING GEAR STRUT ASSEMBLY. IT ALSO APPEARED THAT THE SHOCK ABSORBER ASSEMBLY HAD NOT BEEN PROPERLY ASSEMBLED DURING ITS PREVIOUS OVERHAUL OR MAINTENANCE WHILE THE AIRCRAFT UNDERWENT A HEAVY MAINTENANCE CHECK AT THE (MAE) MOBILE AEROSPACE ENGINEERING, MOBILE ALABAMA, REPAIR STATION. THEREFORE IT APPEARS THAT THE IMPROPER ASSEMBLY OF THE SHOCK ABSORBER DURING PREVIOUS MAINTENANCE LED TO ITS IMPROPER INSTALLATION ON THE NOSE LANDING GEAR SHOCK STRUT ASSEMBLY. IN ADDITION ALL OF THE DAMAGED NOSE LANDING GEAR COMPONENTS AND THOSE THAT WERE SUSPECT WERE REPLACED AND QUARANTINED AS PART OF THE UNITED AIRLINES INVESTIGATION. ALL OF THE REPLACED PARTS WERE SENT TO THE UNITED AIRLINES SHOPS IN SAN FRANCISCO FOR FURTHER INSPECTION AND EVALUATION AS PART OF UNITED AIRLINES OWN CONTINUING INVESTIGATION. AS THE LEFT WING CAME UP, THE PUT APPLIED FULL AILERON DEFLECTION INTO THE LEFT WING. 20021222035019I	(-23) IT IS THE OPINION OF THE TANDEM SYSTEM MANUFACTURER THAT THIS INCIDENT WAS CAUSED BY A PREMATURE DEPLOYMENT OF THE DROGUE AS THE TANDEM PAIR LEFT THE AIRCRAFT. THE PREMATURE DEPLOYMENT WAS MOST LIKELY CAUSED BY THE DROGUE SNAGGING ON A SEAT BELT ATTACH POINT AS THE PARACHUTIST IN COMMAND SLID ON THE FLOOR OF THE AIRCRAFT, IN A SEATED POSITION, TOWARD THE DOOR OF THE AIRCRAFT. ONCE THE TANDEM PAIR EXITED, THE DROGUE BRIDLE WRAPPED SEVERAL TIMES AROUND THE PARACHUTIST IN COMMANDS LEFT LEG BEFORE THE PARACHUTIST IN COMMAND COULD GAIN STABILITY. THIS RESULTED IN A SITUATION WHERE THE DROGUE COULD NOT BE RELEASED, EVEN THOUGH BOTH DROGUE RELEASE HANDLES WERE PULLED. IT ALSO RESULTED IN AN UNCONTROLLABLE SPIN THAT, WHEN THE RESERVE RIPCORD WAS PULLED, CAUSED THE RESERVE FREEBAG BRIDLE TO WRAP AROUND THE DROGUE BRIDAL WHICH ALSO PREVENTED RESERVED DEPLOYMENT. THE FAA CONCURS WITH THIS SYNOPSIS. THE AUTOMATICE ACTIVATION DEVICE (AAD) WAS SENT TO THE MANUFACTURER FOR EXAMINATION AND WAS FOUND TO HAVE OPERATED CORRECTLY. THE ONLY EYEWITNESS TO THIS INCIDENT WAS THE PILOT WHO STATED "I HEARD A FUNNY NOISE LIKE FABRIC RUBBING AGAINST ITSELF AND NOTICED SOMETHING WHITE IN THE DOOR WHICH WENT UNDER THE TAIL". "I OBSERVED THE TANDEM PAIR AS THEY LEFT THE AIRCRAFT AND WHILE IN FREEFALL, ALL OF WHICH LOOKED ABNORMAL. INSTEAD OF DOING JUST ONE TURN TO WATCH THE JUMPERS I DID APPROXIMATELY FOUR TURNS." POST INCIDENT EXAMINATION OF THE TANDEM SYSTEM SHOWED THAT THERE WAS A WHITE DROGUE INSTALLED AND THAT THERE WAS SOME OTHER WHITE MATERIAL IN THE TANDEM SYSTEM WHICH INCLUDED THE MAIN AND RESERVE PARACHUTE SUSPENSION LINES, THE RESERVE FREEBAG, AND THE RESERVE PILOT CHUTE BRIDLE. UNDER NORMAL PROCEDURES, THE UNICOM OPERATOR WOULD LOG THE CALL SIGN OF AIRCRAFT USING THE AIRPORT. ON THE DAY OF THE ACCIDENT, DUE TO THE VOLUME OF TRAFFIC, THE LOG WAS NOT USED. THE UNICOM OPERATOR DID NOT RECALL HEARING THE CESSNA ON FREQUENCY. PRELIMINARY VISUAL EXAMINATION OF THE CESSNA'S TWO DAMAGED COMMUNICATION RADIOS REVEALED THE TOP RADIO WAS INDICATING 122.7, AND THE OTHER WAS 121.902 MHZ. NEAR DEPARTURE END OF THE RUNWAY LOOKED LEFT TO SEE ANY TRAFFIC IN LEFT BREAK ON DOWN WIND LEG. AT ABOUT 1706Z, I REQUESTED MY IFR CLEARANCE AND TAXIED TO THE RUN-UP AREA. DURING THE RUN-UP I FOUND NOTHING UNUSUAL WITH THE AIRCRAFT. I TOOK OFF, HEADED SOUTH AND THE FIRST 40 MINUTES OF THE FLIGHT WERE UNREMARKABLE. SHORTLY AFTER MACON, I TURNED MY FUEL PUMPS ON, AND SWITCHED MY FUEL SELECTOR VALVES FROM THE MAINS TO THE AUXILIARY, WAITING ABOUT TWO MINUTES BETWEEN ENGINES. SOMEWHERE BETWEEN APPROXIMATELY FIVE AND TEN MINUTES AFTERSWITCHING FUEL TANKS, I LOST POWER FROM THE LEFT ENGINE. THE RPM GAUGE SHOWED THAT THE PROPELLER SPEED WAS VERY ERRATIC BETWEEN 1600 AND 2900 RPM SLIGHTLY OVERSPEED AT TIMES. MY INITIAL IMPRESSION WAS THAT A MAG ON THE LEFT ENGINE HAD GONE BAD AGAIN. WE HAD JUST LOST A MAG ON THAT ENGINE THE PREVIOUS WEEK AND HAD IT REPLACED. THE INITIAL SYMPTOMS APPEARED TO BE IDENTICAL. HOWEVER, I SWITCHED MY FUEL SELECTOR VALVES BACK TO THE MAIN TANKS AND THERE WAS NO IMPROVEMENT IN PERFORMANCES. I THEN PROCEEDED TO FOLLOW THE EMERGENCY ACTION ITEM CHECKLIST THAT I HAD COMMITTED TO MEMORY. IN THIS AIRCRAFT: AUTOPILOT DISCONNECT; MIXTURES FORWARD; PROPS FORWARD; THROTTLE MAX AVAILABLE POWER; GEAR UP; FLAPS UP; I PROCEEDED TO IDENTIFY AND VERIFY FOR SURE THAT THE LEFT ENGINE HAD FAILED BY USING THE THROTTLE AND DECIDED TO FEATHER IT DUE TO THE ERRATIC RPMS. I THEN PULLED OUT THE EMERGENCY CHECKLIST TO VERIFY THAT I HAD NOT SKIPPED A STEP. I DECIDED NOT TO RESTART THE ENGINE TO PREVENT THE POSSIBILITY OF BEING UNABLE TO FEATHER IT AGAIN. I DECLARED AN EMERGENCY WITH JACKSONVILLE CENTER AND REQUESTED VECTORS TO THE NEAREST AIRPORT AND WAS GIVEN VECTORS TO THE FITZGERALD, GA AIRPORT. I WAS ABOUT 20 MILES AWAY. BEING FULLY AWARE THAT THEY WERE FULL, I SWITCHED THE FUEL SELECTOR VALVES BACK TO THE AUXILIARY TANKS. AS A WAS SETTING UP FOR A THREE TO FOUR MILE MODIFIED BASE (I WAS TRYING TO GET TO THE AIRPORT AS QUICKLY AS POSSIBLE), THE RIGHT ENGINE BEGAN LOSING POWER. SINCE THERE WAS AT LEAST A MILE OF SWAMP AND WOODS IN BETWEEN ME AND THE AIRPORT, SO I OPTED TO LAND IN THE CORNFIELD DIRECTLY STRAIGHT AHEAD TO ASSURE THE SAFETY OF MY FAMILY. I INSTRUCTED MY FAMILY TO ASSUME THE CRASH LANDING POSITION, TO TIGHTEN THEIR SEAT BELTS AND TO PREPARE TO EXIT THE AIRCRAFT AFTER IT COMES TO A COMPLETE STOP. JUST PRIOR TO TOUCH DOWN, I PULLED BOTH MIXTURES TO CUT OFF, FEATHERED THE RIGHT ENGINE, SWITCHED MY FUEL SELECTOR VALVES TO OFF, AND TURNED OFF THE MASTER TO MINIMIZE THE POSSIBILITY OF FIRE. AS I TOUCHED DOWN AS SLOW AS POSSIBLE, IT APPEARED THAT THE AIRPLANE WOULD ROLL OUT WITH NO DAMAGE HOWEVER, A DEER STAND POPPED UP IN FRONT OF ME. I WAS ABLE TO STEER TO THE LEFT OF THE STAND, BUT WHEN I ATTEMPTED TO STEER BACK AWAY FROM SOME PINE SAPLINGS, THE AIRCRAFT SKIDDED IN THE SANDY SOIL, AND WOULD NOT RESPOND TO RUDDER INPUTS. AT THAT POINT THE PLANE STUMBLED OVER A SMALL RIDGE IN THE FIELD AND THE LEFT WING MADE CONTACT WITH A SMALL PINE TREE AND WE NOSED OVER. THE AIRCRAFT DID NOT CATCH ON FIRE. NO ONE WAS INJURED IN THE LEAST. MY ENTIRE FAMILY EXITED THE AIRCRAFT AND WALKED ABOUT TWO MILES TO THE NEAREST ROAD TO GET A RIDE TO THE AIRPORT WHERE WE RECEIVED A RIDE TO FITZGERALD AIRPORT.

INSTRUMENT METEOROLOGICAL CONDITIONS (IMC) PREVAILED AT THE ACCIDENT SITE AT THE TIME OF THE ACCIDENT, AND THE STUDENT PILOT HAD FILED A VISUAL FLIGHT RULES (VFR) FLIGHT PLAN FOR THE FLIGHT. ACCORDING TO THE STUDENT'S FLIGHT INSTRUCTOR, THE STUDENT WAS TO FLY FROM OAHU TO MAUI BY FLYING OVER THE NORTH SHORE OF MOLOKAI AT 3,500 FEET MSL. THE STUDENT WAS UTILIZING AN ISLAND REPORTING METHOD TO REPORT HIS CURRENT AND FORECAST POSITIONS TO AIR TRAFFIC CONTROLLERS AND FLIGHT SERVICE STATIONS (FSS). INITIAL REPORTS FROM THE FEDERAL AVIATION ADMINISTRATION, INDICATE THAT THE STUDENT HAD SPOKEN WITH THE MOLOKAI AIR TRAFFIC CONTROL TOWER. THE STUDENT WAS INSTRUCTED TO CONTACT HONOLULU RADIO AFTER LEAVING THE MOLOKAI CONTROL AREA; HOWEVER, THE FSS NEVER RECEIVED THE PILOT'S NEXT POSITION REPORT (WHICH WAS SUPPOSED TO BE OVER CAPE HALAWA ON THE EAST SIDE OF THE ISLAND). WHEN THE FSS DID NOT RECEIVE THE NEXT RADIO CALL FROM THE STUDENT, THEY ISSUED AN "ALERT NOTICE (ALNOT)" FOR A MISSING AIRCRAFT. THE U.S. COAST GUARD STARTED SEARCH AND RESCUE MISSION FLIGHTS APPROXIMATELY 1400. INTERVIEWS WITH THE COAST GUARD PILOTS, WHO INITIATED THE SEARCH EFFORTS, REPORTED THEY ENCOUNTERED VISUAL METEOROLOGICAL CONDITIONS (VMC) FROM HONOLULU TO THE WEST SIDE OF MOLOKAI. THEY OBSERVED HAZIER VISIBILITY CONDITIONS WHEN THEY NEARED THE NORTHWEST SIDE OF THE ISLAND. THE PILOTS REPORTED ENCOUNTERING INSTRUMENT METEOROLOGICAL CONDITIONS (IMC) ONCE THEY PASSED HALFWAY OVER THE ISLAND, WITH CLOUD CEILINGS AROUND 500 FEET AND VISIBILITY BETWEEN 1-2 MILES. WEATHER HAMPERED SEARCH EFFORTS UNTIL JANUARY 27, 2003, WHEN A MAUI FIRE DEPARTMENT HELICOPTER SPOTTED THE WRECKAGE ON THE WEST SLOPE OF THE MANUAHI RIDGE. THE WRECKAGE WAS LOCATED APPROXIMATELY 1,500 FEET ABOVE SEA LEVEL, APPROXIMATELY 75 FEET BELOW THE CREST OF THE RIDGE. REVIEW OF THE FLIGHT SCHOOL RENTAL RECORDS REVEALED THAT THE STUDENT HAD ACCUMULATED APPROXIMATELY 34 TOTAL FLIGHT HOURS. THE BURNING DRAIN LINE THEN IGNITED HYDRAULIC FLUID THAT HAD  ACCUMULATED IN THE LOWER AREA OF THE RIGHT SIDE PANEL, WHICH THEN CAUSED THE FAILURE OF THE RIGHT BRAKE HYDRAULIC LINE.

20030401005799I	(-23) ON APRIL 1, 2003, AIRCRAFT N175UA, OPERATING AS UA FLT 896-1 HKG TO ORD DECLARED AN EMERGENCY ON DESCENT AND APPROACH INTO ORD DUE TO A RESTRICTION IN THE ABILITY TO ROLL THE AIRPLANE TO THE LEFT WITH THE CONTROL WHEE. THE CREW WAS CLEARED FOR A LONG STRAIGHT IN APPROACH TO RUNWAY 14R AND HAD AN UNEVENTFUL LANDING AND ROLLOUT. AFTER TAXIING INTO THE GATE, THE CREW WAS ABLE TO OPERATE THE CONTROL WHEEL IN BOTH DIRECTIONS WITH NO RESTRICTIONS. ABOUT 4 HOURS OUTSIDE OF ORD THEY NOTED THAT THEIR PORTABLE WATER TANKS WERE EMPTY AND THAT WATER WAS DRAINING INTO THE PASSENGER CABIN FROM THE CEILING ALONG THE RIGHT HAND AISLE, BETWEEN DOORS 2R AND 3R. UPON PARKING AT THE GATE, THE AIRCRAFT HAD A SIGNIFICANT AMOUNT OF WATER DRAINING FROM THE FUSELAGE DRAIN MASTS AND THE MAIN DECK FLOOR BETWEEN DOOR 2R AND 3R WAS COMPLETELY SATURATED. THE UPPER DECK CART LIFT SHAFT HAD WATER ALONG THE BASE ON THE MAIN DECK. ONCE THE AIRCRAFT ARRIVED IN THE HANGAR, THE TROUBLESHOOTING PLAN FOCUSED ON THE POSSIBILITY THAT THE AILERON CONTROL EVENT AND THE WATER DRAINAGE ISSUE COULD BE RELATED. IT WAS THEORIZED THAT THIS COULD HAVE BEEN THE RESULT OF WATER FREEZING ON THE AILERON CONTROL CABLES IN THE MAIN LANDING GEAR WHEEL WELL, BASED ON SIMILAR IN-FLIGHT EVENTS FROM OTHER OPERATORS AS PER BOEING SERVICE BULLETIN 747-51A2057, INSPECTION OF THE "CANTED PRESSURE DECK DRAINAGE SYSTEM." DURING THE ISOLATION AND TROUBLESHOOTING OF A POSSIBLE WATER LEAK IN THE PASSENGER CABIN AREA AND THE UPPER DECK GALLEY, THE FOLLOWING CIRCUIT BREAKERS ON THE P414 PANEL IN THE E&E (ELECTRICAL/ELECTRONIC COMPARTMENT) WERE FOUND OPEN AND NOT TAGGED: 1. 414L22 FWD DRAIN MAST HEATER AIR MODE 2. 414L23 CENTER DRAIN MAST HEATER AIR MODE 3. 414L24 AFT DRAIN MAST HEATER AIR MODE 4. 414C21 DRAIN MAST HEATER GROUND MODE THE ABOVE NOTED CIRCUIT BREAKERS WERE PULLED AS PART OF A MAINTENANCE TASK TO SUPPORT THE CLEANING OF THE OVERBOARD DRAIN LINES TO THE AIRCRAFT EXTERIOR DRAIN MAST. THIS WAS ACCOMPLISHED AT HKG (HONG KONG) ON MARCH 31, 2003. DURING THE SUBSEQUENT TROUBLESHOOTING BY MAINTENANCE AND ENGINEERING IT WAS NOTED THAT WHEN THE DRAIN MASTS WERE PLUGGED (SIMULATING A FROZEN CONDITION), WATER BACKED UP THROUGH THE UPPER DECK GALLEY CHILLER DRAIN AND BEGAN TO OVERFLOW INTO THE CABIN THROUGH THE CEILING PANELS ALONG THE RIGHT HAND AISLE IN BUSINESS CLASS. THIS WATER WOULD EVENTUALLY WORK ITS WAY DOWN TO THECENTER FUSELAGE UNDER FLOOR AREA AND INTO THE CANTED PRESSURE DECK AREA THAT ALSO SERVES LIKE A SUMP AREA. IN ADDITION DURING THE INSPECTION AND TROUBLESHOOTING, THE MAIN LANDING GEAR WHEEL WELL DRAINS THAT LEAD FROM THE CANTED PRESSURE DECK AREA WERE FOUND TO BE CLEAN AND CLEAR BUT A 6" X 0.125" GAP WAS FOUND ON THE RIGHT SIDE ALONG THE OUTBOARD EDGE OF THE CANTED PRESSURE BULKHEAD PANEL AT RBL 100. THIS GAP WAS DUE TO A LACK OF SEALANT AND WOULD ALLOW ANY ACCUMULATED WATER TO BE FORCED OUT BY CABIN PRESSURE. ONCE FORCED OUT AS A SPRAY INTO THE RIGHT WHEEL WELL, THE WATER WOULD COAT AND FREEZE ON THE AILERON CONTROL CABLES THAT ARE POSITIONED ON THE AFT SIDE OF THIS BULKHEAD PANEL. MAINTENANCE SUBSEQUENTLY RESEALED THE CANTED PRESSURE BULKHEAD AT RBL 100, WHICH WAS DETERMINED TO BE THE REASON FOR WATER SPRAYING ONTO THE AILERON CABLES. THE DRAIN MAST CIRCUIT BREAKERS WERE ALSO RESET AND NO LEAKS WERE EVER FOUND IN THE POTABLE WATER SYSTEM TO EXPLAIN WHY THE TANKS WERE EMPTY AS ORIGINALLY NOTED BY THE AIRCREW. MAINTENANCE AND ENGINEERING SPECULATE THAT THE TANKS MAY NOT HAVE BEEN FULL TO BEGIN WITH AND THE REMAINING WATER WAS CONSUMED NORMALLY. IN CONCLUSION THE AIRCRAFT WAS RETURNED TO ITS NORMAL CONFIGURATION AND A VERIFICATION TEST FLIGHT WAS FLOWN ON APRIL 4, 2003. THE AIRCRAFT WAS FLOWN FOR 3 HOURS WITH MINIMUM CONTROL INPUTS ON A CONSTANT HEADING FOR AN APPROXIMATE SIMULATION OF THE ORIGINAL PROBLEM FLIGHT. THE TEST FLIGHT WAS SATISFACTORY WITH NO DISCREPANCIES NOTED. AS TO THE PROBLEM OF THE DRAIN MAST CIRCUIT BREAKERS,^PRIVACY DATA OMITTED^

20030413011929A	(-23) DURING A FLIGHT THAT WAS TO BE AN IFR TRAINING FLIGHT DEPARTING FROM SEDONA TO WILLIAMS GATEWAY A BEECH BONANZA A-36 WAS DESTROYED AFTER FAILING TO GET AIRBORNE AFTER TAKEOFF. THE AIRCRAFT HAD THREE PEOPLE ON BOARD: A PRIVATE PILOT, THE INSTRUCTOR, AND ONE OBSERVER IN THE BACK SEAT. WITNESSES ON THE AIRPORT HAD OBSERVED THE AIRCRAFT ON THE RUNWAY ATTEMPTING TO TAKEOFF WITHOUT ENOUGH POWER. THE AIRCRAFT CONTINUED DOWN THE RUNWAY UNTIL IT WAS OBSERVED THE AIRCRAFT ROTATED 4/5 DOWN THE RUNWAY, THE WITNESS OBSERVED THAT THE ATTITUDE OF THE AIRCRAFT WAS HIGH BUT THE MAINS WERE STILL ON THE RUNWAY. AT THE END OF THE RUNWAY THE AIRCRAFT LIFTED ABOUT 2 TO 3 FEET IN AN EXTREME NOSE HIGH ATTITUDE. THE AIRPORT BOUNDARY AT THE END OF THE RUNWAY DROPS OFF TO A SHEAR CLIFF OF 400 FEET. THE AIRCRAFT THEN CONTINUED INTO THE RAVINE AND IMPACTED THE OPPOSITE BANK IN AN APPARENT STALL AND WAS DESTROYED BY FIRE. ALL ON BOARD PERISHED. INTERVIEWS WITH THE WITNESSES, INCLUDING SOME PILOTS WHO HAD EXPERIENCE IN THIS AIRCRAFT TYPE, STATED THAT IT WAS OBVIOUS TO THEM THAT THE AIRCRAFT WAS NOT PRODUCING ENOUGH POWER. THE ENGINE WAS NOT RUNNING ROUGH, JUST THAT THE RPM SEEMED LOW. AN EVALUATION OF THE ENGINE REVEALED THAT THE SPARK PLUGS HAD EVIDENCE OF LEAN CONDITION. THE POWERPLANT REPRESENTATIVE HAD EXAMINED THE ENGINE AND CONFIRMED THAT THE FUEL SYSTEM USED A COMPENSATING ANEROID, THIS MEANT THAT THE ENGINE SHOULD NOT HAVE BEEN LEANED FOR TAKEOFF AT A HIGH ALTITUDE AIRPORT. AN INTERVIEW WITH OTHER STUDENTS AND INSTRUCTORS WHOM HAD FLOWN WITH THE INSTRUCTOR IN THE ACCIDENT AIRCRAFT REVEALED THAT SHE WOULD TEACH LEANING IN THIS AND THE OTHER BONANZA. THE SECOND BONANZA OPERATED BY THE FLIGHT SCHOOL DOES NOT HAVE THE COMPENSATING ANEROID AND WOULD REQUIRE LEANING FOR BEST PERFORMANCE. SOME OTHER FACTORS IN THE ACCIDENT WERE THE CHECKLISTS FOR THE AIRCRAFT DID NOT REQUIRE THAT THIS AIRCRAFT BE FULL RICH FOR TAKEOFF. ALSO THE INSTRUCTOR'S STYLE WAS TO LET THE STUDENT MAKE MINOR MISTAKES AND ALLOW THE STUDENT TO DISCOVER THE ERROR ON THEIR OWN. THE TIME BETWEEN THE STUDENT NOTICING THE ERROR AND THE TIME NEEDED TO ABORT THE TAKEOFF WAS TOO SHORT; HOWEVER, MANIFOLD PRESSURE AND RPM PROBLEMS SHOULD HAVE BEEN EVIDENT. THIS FLIGHT SCHOOL HAD ALREADY CHANGED ITS TRAINING PROCEDURES TO INCLUDE MORE AIRCRAFT SPECIFIC OPERATIONS OF SYSTEMS AND ALSO MORE INSTRUCTIONS FOR GO-NO GO DECISIONS, AND TO BE MORE AGGRESSIVE IN MAKING THOSE DECISIONS EARLY ENOUGH IN THE TAKEOFF ROLL. TESTS WERE PERFORMED IN FARMINTON NM IN A SIMILAR AIRCRAFT WITH SIMILAR CONDITIONS. SEVERAL PROFILES WERE TESTED TO DETERMINE IF THE FUEL MIXTURE SETTING AND THE RPM SETTINGS WOULD CONTRIBUTE TO THIS ACCIDENT. IT WAS DISCOVERED THAT THE AIRCRAFT WOULD IN EVERY CASE REACH FLYING SPEED NO MATTER HOW THE MIXTURE AND PROPELLER SETTINGS WERE USED. THE ONLY SCENARIO THAT BEST LOOKED LIKE WHAT WITNESSES HAD OBSERVED WAS TO TRY AND TAKEOFF WITH THE RPM SET AT CRUISE (2300), THE MIXTURE CONTROL SET TO LEAN, AND THE FLAPS SET TO FULL DOWN. THE FLAPS IN THE WRECKAGE WAS FOUND IN THE 5-DEGREE POSITION. IT COULD NOT BE DETERMINED IF THE FLAPS WERE IN TRANSIT LATER IN THE TAKEOFF ROLL. IT COULD BE POSSIBLE THAT IF THE FLAPS WERE SET TO FULL DOWN AND DISCOVERED TOO LATE IN THE AIRCRAFT ROLL TO ABORT BEFORE THE END OF THE RUNWAY. THE INSTRUCTOR COULD HAVE TRIED TO RETRACT THE FLAPS AT THE LAST MINUTE. THIS COULD ACCOUNT FOR THE SETTLING THAT WITNESSES HAD SEEN. ALL THOSE FACTORS NOTWITHSTANDING, THERE STILL WAS THE ISSUE THAT IT WAS OBVIOUS TO THE WITNESSES THAT THE AIRCRAFT WAS NOT PERFORMING AS EXPECTED AND THE PILOTS CONTINUED WITH THE TAKEOFF ANYWAY.

20030417007029A	(-23) AIRCRAFT LOST POWER AFTER TAKEOFF. ENGINE WENT TO UNCOMMANDED 70% POWER. PILOT DUMPED LOAD, MADE EMERGENCY LANDING IN CULTIVATED FIELD. RESULTED IN SUBSTANTIAL DAMAGE TO AIRCRAFT. NO INJURIES TO THE PILOT. ACCIDENT SITE WAS PHOTOGRAPHED BY THE OWNER BEFORE THE AIRCRAFT WAS RETURNED TO THE HANGAR. VISUAL INSPECTION OF THE ENGINE REVEALED THAT THE PRIMARY FUEL TRANSFER TUBE, PART NUMBER (P/N) 3011155 LOCATED BETWEEN THE NUMBER 5 AND 6 FUEL MANIFOLD ADAPTER ASSEMBLIES WAS NOT IN ITS PROPER POSITION. VISUAL INSPECTION WITH A MIRROR SHOWED THAT THE "O" RING WAS PROTRUDING OUTSIDE OF THE ADAPTER ON THE LOWER SIDE. FUEL LEAKAGE AT THIS TUBE WAS CONFIRMED BY RUNNING THE ENGINE IN THE "AS FOUND" CONDITION AND OBSERVING A SEVERE LEAK WHILE THE ENGINE WOULD NOT DEVELOP POWER ABOVE 72%NG. WHEN THE TUBE WAS RE-POSITIONED, THE LEAK WAS NOT OBSERVED AND THE ENGINE DEVELOPED FULL POWER. THESE ENGINE RUNS WERE OBSERVED BY QUALIFIED MECHANICS, PILOTS AND FAA PERSONNEL. INSPECTION OF THE ENTIRE FUEL MANIFOLD INSTALLATION SHOWED THAT THE TRANSFER TUBE LOCK PLATES (P/N 3011158) AT NOZZLE'S 4 AND 8 WERE SLIGHTLY DISTORTED. THE SECONDARY TRANSFER TUBE BETWEEN THE NUMBER 4 AND 5 ADAPTER WAS NOT SEATED PROPERLY. AT THIS POSITION, THE LOCK PLATE WAS RESTING ON THE SHOULDER OF THE TUBE RATHER THAN IN THE GROOVE. ADDITIONALLY IT WAS NOTED THAT THE IGNITERS WERE SAFETIED TO THEIR ADJACENT LOCK PLATES. A REVIEW OF THE MAINTENANCE RECORDS FOR THE AIRCRAFT SHOWED THAT THE NOZZLES HAD BEEN INSTALLED AND FUNCTIONING PROPERLY SINCE 12/20/2002 AND HAD ACCUMULATED 110.7 HOURS IN SERVICE SINCE THAT TIME. THE ENGINE HAD RECEIVED A 100 HOUR VISUAL INSPECTION ON 04/08/2003 WHICH INCLUDED AN ENGINE COMPARTMENT CLEAING, ENGINE RUN-UP AND POST RUN-UP INSPECTION FOR LEAKS. NO LEAKS NOTED. NO ABNORMAL CONDITIONS WERE OBSERVED. AT THE TIME OF THE ACCIDENT THE AIRCRAFT HAD ACCUMULATED 3.9 HOURS SINCE THIS 100 HOUR INSPECTION. FOLLOW UP INSPECTION WITH THE REPAIR STATION THAT PERFORMED THE LAST FUEL NOZZLE REMOVAL AND REINSTALLATION ON 12/20/2002 SHOWED THAT THEIR STOCK OF SERVICEABLE LOCK PLATES CONTAINED NUMEROUS DISTORTED PLATES. THE WORSE CASE WAS USED TO DEMONSTRATE THAT IT COULD STILL BE INSTALLED CORRECTLY AND IT WOULD ADEQUATELY RETAIN THE TRANSFER TUBES. HOWEVER, THE LOCK PLATES DID NOT CONTACT 100% OF THE TRANSFER TUBE SHOULDER AND THEY DID NOT NEST PROPERLY AND FULLY IN THE TRANSFER TUBE GROOVE. REVIEW OF PRATT & WHITNEY OVERHAUL DATA DID NOT INDICATE ANY INSPECTION CRITERIA TO BE USED WHEN INSPECTING THE LOCK PLATES FOR SERVICEABILITY. OPERATING HISTORY OF THIS ENGINE INDICATES THAT THIS IS AN ISOLATED OCCURRENCE. TO PRECLUDE A RECURRENCE OF THIS CONDITION IT IS RECOMMENDED THAT: THE ENGINE MANUFACTURER ESTABLISH INSPECTION CRITERIA FOR THE LOCK PLATES WITH PARTICULAR EMPHASIS ON DISTORTION OF THE LOCK PLATE FLANGES. CRITERIA TO BE USED DURING OVERHAUL OR ANY TIME PLATES ARE REMOVED AND RE-INSTALLED. ADD A CAUTION NOTE TO THE LOCKING PLATE REMOVAL PROCEDURE LOCATED IN P&WC MAINTENANCE 3021242, CHAPTER 73-10-05, PAGE 202, ITEM B, (3), ALERTING MAINTENANCE PERSONNEL NOT TO PRY THE PLATES LOOSE CAUSING THEM TO BEND AND BECOME DISTORTED.

THE AIRCRAFT IMPACTED THE "G" TAXIWAY ADJACENT TO THE GENERAL AVIATION "T" HANGARS. THE FIRST POINT OF CONTACT APPEARS TO HAVE BEEN THE LEFT HAND WING TIP FUEL TANK, WHICH DEPARTED THE AIRCRAFT AND WAS COMPROMISED. THIS PROVIDED AN AEROSOL FLAMMABLE, WHICH WAS IGNITED AND CAUSED A SUBSTANTIAL AMOUNT OF HEAT DAMAGE TO THE LEFT SIDE AND PORTIONS OF THE BELLY OF THE AIRCRAFT. THE LEFT TO RIGHT (NEARLY 90 DEG.) BENDING MOMENT OF THE NOSE ASSEMBLY VALIDATED THE LEFT WING AND NOSE LOW IMPACT SCENARIO, WHICH APPEARS TO HAVE BEEN THE SECOND POINT OF CONTACT DURING THE IMPACT. THE AIRCRAFT APPEARS TO HAVE REBOUNDED FROM THE INITIAL IMPACT AND SUBSEQUENTLY SLID ON ITS BELLY SOUTHEASTERLY DOWN TAXIWAY "G" APPROX. 972 FEET FROM THE FIRST NOTABLE GROUND SCARS TO THE FINAL STOPPING POINT. BOTH PROPELLER ASSEMBLIES WERE BROKEN THROUGH THEIR RESPECTIVE HUBS AND ALL BUT ONE BLADE ON THE LEFT ASSEMBLY WERE SEPARATED FROM THE HUBS DURING THE CRASH ATTENUATION. STRIKES ON THE ADVANCING BLADE EDGES WITH CORRESPONDING "STRIATIONS" ACROSS THE BLADE FACES WERE INDICATIVE OF "ROTATION" OR OTHERWISE UNDER POWER BUT THE STRIKE SIGNATURES ALSO INDICATED A "LOW POWER" SIGNATURE. DURING DOCUMENTATION OF THE COCKPIT THIS APPEARS TO CORRESPOND WITH THE THROTTLE LEVER POSITION OF BOTH IN "IDLE". THIS DID NOT APPEAR TO BE A POST ACCIDENT ANOMALY AS THE LEFT THROTTLE LEVER WAS "STUCK" IN THIS POSITION AND THE RIGHT WAS ADJACENT TO IT AND MOVED FREELY. THE COCKPIT APPEARED TO BE CONFIGURED PROPERLY FOR A "TAKE-OFF" WITH PROPELLERS IN "LOW PITCH, HIGH RPM", MIXTURES IN "FULL RICH" AND AUX. FUEL PUMPS SELECTED IN "LOW". ALL ELECTRICAL AND IGNITION SWITCHES APPEARED TO BE PROPERLY SELECTED AND NO CIRCUIT BREAKERS WERE FOUND IN AN "OPEN" POSITION. INITIAL WRECKAGE INSPECTION INDICATED THAT THERE WAS "FLIGHT CONTROL CONTINUITY" THROUGH ALL AXES' AND THIS WAS LATER CONFIRMED DURING A MORE DETAILED INSPECTION IN CONCERT WITH A REPRESENTATIVE OF THE CESSNA CORPORATION'S ACCIDENT INVESTIGATION OFFICE. NOTED WAS THE APPEARANCE THAT THE LANDING GEAR ASSEMBLIES WERE NOT IN A "DOWN AND LOCKED" CONFIGURATION ALBEIT THE SELECTOR SWITCH WAS SELECTED IN THE "DOWN" POSITION. IT WAS VALIDATED DURING THE DETAILED INSPECTION THAT THE GEAR WAS ACTUALLY "IN TRANSIT" AND NOT "LOCKED" AT THE TIME OF THE ACCIDENT. PRELIMINARY INSPECTION OF THE FLAP DRIVE ASSEMBLIES ALSO INDICATE THEY MAY HAVE BEEN IN AN APPROXIMATELY 12 DEG. DOWN POSITION (THIS IS TO BE REVALIDATED AT A LATER DATE) POSSIBLY HAVING BEEN SELECTED DOWN FOR LANDING. TO THE EXTENT POSSIBLE, THE FUEL SUPPLY SYSTEMS WERE EXAMINED TO THE "FLOW DIVIDERS" OF BOTH POWERPLANTS. THE AIRCRAFT LEFT THE RUNWAY JUST NORTH OF THE INTERSECTION WITH RUNWAY 07-25, AS THE AIRCRAFT ENCOUNTERED SOFT SOIL, THE NOSE GEAR COLLAPSED CAUSING A WRINKLE IN THE FUSELAGE JUST FORWARD OF THE COPILOTS WINDSHIELD EXTENDING TO THE RIGHT HAND WING ROOT AREA AND DAMAGE TO RIGHT AND LEFT HAND PROPELLERS. NO INJURIES TO THE PILOT, WHO WAS ALONE IN THE AIRCRAFT, NO POST ACCIDENT FIRE. AN INSPECTION OF THE AIRCRAFT ON 05-20-2003, WHILE TIED DOWN ON THE RAMP NEAR THE FIRE STATION FOUND THE NOSE GEAR EXTEND/RETRACT LINKS BROKE AND BENT. ALSO, THE NOSE GEAR STEERING ARM (P/N 44387-00) TO BE MISSING (NOT FOUND ON RUNWAY OR AT ACCIDENT SITE) AND NOSE GEAR HOUSING ASSEMBLY (P/N 40273-00) WITH DEFORMED RIGHT TURN LIMIT STOP BENT ALLOWING OVER STEERING TO THE RIGHT TO APPROXIMATELY 80 DEGREES OF TRAVEL. IN MY OPINION, THIS ACCIDENT RESULTED FROM AN OVERSTEERING INCIDENT, PROBABLY BY A GROUND HANDLING TUG. THE OVERSTEERING CAUSED SHEAR STRESS ON THE STEERING ARM ATTACH BOLTS, ALLOWING THEM TO FAIL AND CAUSE A CONDITION WHERE THE PILOT WAS UNABLE TO CONTROL THE DIRECTION OF THE AIRCRAFT ON THE GROUND, I.E. THE LANDING ROLL OUT AT EAT. ALSO THE OVERSTEERING CAUSED THE RIGHT STEERING STOP ON THE UPPER STRUT HOUSING TO FAIL ALLOWING THE STRUT TO EASILY EXCEED THE RIGHT HAND TURNING LIMIT DURING TUGGING OPERATIONS THUS, REPEATEDLY LOADING THE STEERING ARM ATTACH BOLTS TO BE PUT UNDER A SHEAR STRESS LOAD. ON THIS AIRCRAFT, THE RIGHT HAND TURNING LIMIT STOP HAD BEEN BROKEN PREVIOUSLY. A WELD REPAIR HAD BEEN MADE, WHICH WAS BROKEN AT THE TIME I LOOKED AT THIS AIRCRAFT ON 05-20-03. THERE IS NO APPROVAL FOR THIS WELDED REPAIR. IN MY OPINION, THE STEERING STOP FAILURE WAS EXISTING AT THE TIME THE AIRCRAFT TAXIED FOR TAKE OFF AT SPOKANE, WA (GEG). DUE TO A LACK OF A PREFLIGHT INSPECTION OR A LACK OF PREFLIGHT INSPECTION KNOWLEDGE ON BEHALF OF THE PILOT, THE STEERING STOP FAILURE WENT UNDETECTED. THIS FAILURE HAS PROBABLY EXISTED FOR SOME TIME AND WAS NOT ADDRESSED BY COMPANY MAINTENANCE. IT WOULD APPEAR THAT PERFORMING JUST ANNUAL INSPECTIONS RATHER THAN 100 HR INSPECTIONS AND ANNUALS IS INADEQUATE FOR THE TYPE OF OPERATION AND THE NUMBER OF HOURS FLOWN BY THIS OPERATOR.

IN THE AIR, THE DIRECTIONAL STABILITY ISSUES WORSENED, AND WHEN A TURN WAS ATTEMPTED, THE AIRCRAFT WOULD SKID, MAKING CONTROL DIFFICULT. DURING THE SHORT FLIGHT, MR. HYDE WAS UNABLE TO EFFECTIVELY CONTROL THE AIRCRAFT, WHICH THEN STRUCK THE TREES, DAMAGING THE AIRCRAFT AND INJURING THE PILOT.

THE AIRCRAFT AND NAME BECAME INSTANTLY RECOGNIZABLE WHEN I APPROACHED THE AIRCRAFT BECAUSE OF AN ACCIDENT INVESTIGATION I HAD CONDUCTED IN 2001 AT THE LACROSSE, WI, AIRPORT INVOLVING THE AIRCRAFT AND MR. TERRY MCILRATH THE APPARENT OCCUPANT. THE AIRCRAFT HAD DUAL CONTROLS, AND IT IS NOT KNOWN FOR CERTAIN WHO THE PILOT-IN-COMMAND WAS. I AM ASSUMING THAT THE INDIVIDUALS WERE IN THE APPROPRIATE SEATS, THUS MR. STUART MERTON MCILRATH WOULD HAVE BEEN THE PILOT. THE ACCIDENT SCENE WAS INSTANTLY RECOGNIZABLE AS A STALL SPIN. WRECKAGE WAS GROUPED IN A TIGHT PATTERN WITH THE TAIL POINTING UP AND KINKED OVER TO WEST. FLIGHT INSTRUMENTS INDICATED THAT THE AIRCRAFT HAD IMPACTED THE EARTH INVERTED AND IN A LEFT WING LOW AND A 30 DEGREES OR MORE NOSE DOWN PITCH ATTITUDE (THIS IS CONSISTENT WITH EYE WITNESS ACCOUNTS). IT WAS REPORTED THAT THE AIRCRAFT PITCHED UP AND THEN DOVE TO THE GROUND WHILE TURNING 1-1/2 TIMES BEFORE IMPACTING THE EARTH. I WAS NOT ABLE TO ASCERTAIN THE AIRSPEED. THE MANIFOLD PRESSURE GAUGE READ 31 INCHES OF MANIFOLD PRESSURE. THERE WAS EVIDENCE OF A SIGNIFICANT FUEL SPILL INDICATING THAT ADEQUATE FUEL WAS ON BOARD THE AIRCRAFT. AIRCRAFT DAMAGE WAS SO SEVERE IT WAS DIFFICULT TO DETERMINE IF THE ENGINE WAS DEVELOPING POWER AT THE TIME OF IMPACT. ALL OF THE PROPELLER BLADES WERE BROKEN OFF APPROXIMATELY 11 INCHES OUT FROM THE HUB AND DID NOT SHOW SIGNS OF IMPACT; HOWEVER, ONE BLADE WAS LOCATED APPROXIMATELY 150 FEET FROM THE ACCIDENT SCENE NORTH AND EAST OF THE ACCIDENT SITE ON THE OTHER SIDE OF THE ROAD. THERE WAS CONTINUITY WITH THE CONTROLS AND THE CONTROL SURFACES. THE WEATHER ON JULY 5, 2003, AT TOMA, WISCONSIN, AT 0912 HOURS WAS CLEAR WITH UNRESTRICTED VISIBILITY AND CALM WINDS. BOTH BODIES WERE SENT FOR AUTOPSY, AND IT IS THE OPINION OF THE ATTENDING PHYSICIAN THAT HEART ATTACK AND STROKE FOR BOTH OCCUPANTS WAS NOT LIKELY A CAUSAL FACTOR. THERE WERE POWER LINES CLOSER TO THE ACCIDENT SITE TO THE WEST PARALLELING THE ROAD. THE DISCOVERY OF A 1/4-INCH TEAR IN THE FUEL PRESSURE REGULATOR (AS REPORTED BY INSPECTOR DERNER) COULD HAVE CAUSED THE ENGINE TO FAIL. IT IS PROBABLE THAT THE PILOT PREPARED FOR AN EMERGENCY LANDING AND DISCOVERED THE POWER LINES. ^PRIVACY DATA OMITTED^ ROBERT K. GESSERT AIRCRAFT PROGRAM MANAGER. THE AIRCRAFT WAS SUBSTANTIALLY DAMAGED, THREE OCCUPANTS RECEIVED MINOR INJURIES, AND ONE RECEIVED SERIOUS INJURIES. DURING THE INVESTIGATION OF THE AIRCRAFT ON SITE, IT WAS NOTED THAT THE LANDING GEAR WAS STILL RETRACTED, THE FLAPS WERE EXTENDED, AND THE MIXTURE CONTROL WAS NOT IN A FULL RICH POSITION. MANY OF THE SWITCHES WERE IN THE OFF POSITION, INCLUDING THE ALTERNATOR FIELD SWITCH, HOWEVER IT WAS NOT POSSIBLE TO DETERMINE THE POSITION OF THESE SWITCHES AT THE TIME OF THE ACCIDENT. WITH THE AIRCRAFT LIFTED AND A JUMP BATTERY CONNECTED, THE LANDING GEAR EXTENDED NORMALLY. A SPECIFIC GRAVITY TEST WAS CONDUCTED ON THE BATTERY REMOVED FROM THE AIRCRAFT AND IT WAS DETERMINED THAT THE BATTERY LACKED ADEQUATE CHARGE TO OPERATE THE ELECTRIC LANDING GEAR MOTOR. THE ALTERNATOR WAS REMOVED AND TESTED FOR PROPER OPERATION WITH NO DISCREPANCIES NOTED. THE WEATHER AT THE TIME OF THE ACCIDENT WAS 10-STATUE MILES VISIBILITY, FEW CLOUDS AT 7500 FEET, AND TEMPERATURE WAS 37 C. ^PRIVACY DATA OMITTED^

BY FAILING TO CHECK THE LIGHTS, THE STAGE WAS SET FOR THE INCIDENT. WE SURMISE THAT THE AIR PUMP WAS SUCKING EXHAUST GASSES THROUGH THE HOLES, BLOWING THEM THROUGH THE CAPTAIN'S GYRO HORIZON AND FIRST OFFICER'S GYRO HORIZON AND DIRECTIONAL GYRO, AND INTO THE COCKPIT. ALTHOUGH ON LOWER ALTITUDE FLIGHTS AND FLIGHTS WITH THE AIR VENTS OPEN, THE CO CONCENTRATION APPARENTLY DID NOT GET HIGH ENOUGH TO CAUSE A PROBLEM (OR DARKEN THE "SPOT" ON THE CO DETECTOR IN THE AIRPLANE), THE LONG CLIMB TO ALTITUDE AND OPERATION WITH THE VENTS SHUT DID SO ON THE DAY OF THE INCIDENT. THE TAILPIPE, INLINE AIR FILTERS, AND GYRO INSTRUMENTS CONNECTED TO THE AIRPLANE'S PNEUMATIC SYSTEM WERE CHANGED. I CONDUCTED A TEST FLIGHT, CLIMBING TO 10,000 MSL. DURING THE LAST 1000 FT OF CLIMB, I CLOSED ALL COCKPIT AIR INLETS AND TURNED THE HEATER ON TO THE FULL HOT POSITION, LEAVING IT IN THAT CONDITION FOR TWO MINUTES AFTER LEVEL-OFF. THERE WERE NO INDICATION OF CO FROM EITHER THE ELECTRONIC OR "DARK SPOT" CO DETECTORS. I THEN RETURNED TO KBUR. AFTER LANDING AND TURNING OFF THE RUNWAY, I OPENED THE CREW DOOR. A GUST OF CROSSWIND BLEW EXHAUST GAS FROM THE LEFT ENGINE IN THROUGH THE OPEN DOOR, AND THE ELECTRONIC CO DETECTOR "BEEPED" - CONFIRMING THAT IT WAS WORKING PROPERLY. THE AIRPLANE WAS RETURNED TO SERVICE AND HAS HAD NO REPORTED CO PROBLEMS SINCE.

AS THE AIRCRAFT TURNED TO TAXI OFF THE RUNWAY FOLLOWING THE LANDING ROLLOUT, THE LINKAGE AGAIN SEPARATED AND DISABLED THE NOSE WHEEL STEERING. CONCLUSIONS: THE ENGINE QUIT DUE TO UNKNOWN CIRCUMSTANCES. THE FIRE WAS STARTED BY AN UNKNOWN SOURCE AND WAS CENTERED IN THE FUEL SHUTOFF VALVE AND GASCOLATOR AREA, ON THE LEFT FORWARD SIDE OF THE AIRCRAFT.

DISCUSSION: UPS MAINTENANCE WORKING WITH UPS TECH SUPPORT IN LOUISVILLE IDENTIFIED THE PROBLEM AS A FAILED RCCB (REMOTE CONTROL CIRCUIT BREAKER) FOR THE "A" PHASE OF AC GENERATOR BUS 1, (ITEM NUMBER B1-174). WHEN THIS BREAKER FAILED ALL COMPONENTS THAT ARE 3 PHASE HAD THEIR PHASE "B" AND "C" CIRCUIT BREAKERS POP. THE RCCB WAS REPLACED AND MAINTENANCE PERFORMED THE APPROPRIATE OPERATIONAL CHECKS AND ALL WAS FOUND TO FUNCTION NORMALLY. BECAUSE THIS OFFICE WAS CONCERNED ABOUT A COMMENT IN THE LOG BOOK WHICH MENTIONED A LOSS OF "#1 COMM" THIS OFFICE REQUESTED THAT UPS MAINTENANCE DUPLICATE THE PROBLEM AND CHECK THE NUMBER 1 VHF FOR PROPER OPERAITON. A CHECK WAS PERFORMED AS REQUESTED AND THE NUMBER 1 VHF COMM FUNCTIONED NORMALLY. THIS OFFICE WOULD LIKE TO POINT OUT THAT THIS TYPE OF FAILURE IS IDENTIFIED IN THE ABNORMALS SECTION OF THE FLIGHT MANUAL. THE CREW FOLLOWED THESE PROCEDURES SUCCESS FULLY. NOTE: THE INITIAL REPORT SENT BY THE ANCHORAGE FSDO MENTIONED "ALL IRUS FAILED" THIS WAS NOT THE CASE. ADVISED THE AIRCRAFT DESIGN WOULD ALLOW CONTROL OF THE AIRCRAFT WITH RUDDER, TILLER AND EMERGENCY BRAKE AND KEEP THE AIRCRAFT ON THE RUNWAY.

THIS SLIDER, MILITARY PART #204-010-720-3 IS A LIFE-LIMITED PART, AND WAS NOT MARKED WITH ANY PART NUMBERS AS REQUIRED BY FAA REGULATION. THERE IS A POSSIBILITY THAT THIS SLIDER IS AN UNAPPROVED PART. THE 90-DEGREE GEARBOX, COMPLETE TAIL ROTOR PITCH ASSEMBLY, AND TAIL ROTOR BLADES WILL BE FORWARDED TO THE NTSB OFFICE SEATLLE, WASHINGTON. HE WAS TRANSPORTED TO THE HOSPITAL, WHERE HE WAS PRONOUNCED DEAD OF BLUNT FORCE TRAUMA TO THE CHEST. AFTER OBSERVING THE ACCIDENT SITE AND ANALYZING THE WEATHER DATA AND THE WITNESSES' STATEMENTS, I FIND IT HIGHLY LIKELY THAT THE BALLOON EXPERIENCED FALSE LIFT, WHICH THE PILOT DID NOT ANTICIPATE NOR PLAN FOR. ONCE HE FOUND HIMSELF IN THE SITUATION, HE WAS UNABLE TO COMPENSATE ADEQUATELY. AN EARLIER DECISION TO OPEN THE VENT AND DESCEND COULD HAVE GREATLY MITIGATED THE DAMAGE AND INJURIES, WHILE ACCEPTING THE CERTAINTY OF THE UPPER PORTION OF THE BALLOON CONTACTING THE WIRES.

MAGNETO DROP ON THE LEFT MAGNETO WAS APPROXIMATELY 100 RPM AND APPROXIMATELY 200 RPM ON THE RIGHT MAGNETO INDICATING A FOULED PLUG OR IMPROPER MAGNETO TIMING. IT IS POSSIBLE THAT POWER WAS REDUCED TO IDLE DURING THE FINAL APPROACH AT WHICH TIME THE ENGINE QUIT DUE TO A LEAN CARBURETOR ADJUSTMENT WITH INSUFFICIENT ALTITUDE REMAINING FOR A RESTART. THE AIRPLANE CAME TO REST APPROXIMATELY 2,800 FEET FROM THE TAKE OFF END OF THE RUNWAY (THE RUNWAY IS 50 X 2,900 FEET, TURF). THE GRASS WAS 8-10 INCHES LONG AT THE TIME OF THE ACCIDENT. INVESTIGATION REVEALED THAT FOUR (4) OF THE EIGHT (8) SPARK PLUGS WERE OIL WET AND WERE LEAD FOULED. THE FOULED PLUGS SHOULD HAVE BEEN DETECTED ON THE ENGINE RUN UP AND MAGNETO CHECK PRIOR TO TAKE OFF. THE ENGINE MAINTENANCE RECORDS INDICATE THAT THE FOUR BOTTOM PLUGS HAD A HISTORY OF FOULING. WITH THE FOUR (4) FOULED OUT SPARK PLUGS IT WAS NOT POSSIBLE FOR THE ENGINE TO DEVELOP FULL POWER AND WOULD CAUSE THE "CHUGGING" NOISE THAT THE WITNESSES HEARD. EVIDENCE FOUND DURING THE INVESTIGATION SUPPORTS WHAT THE WITNESSES STATED. THAT THE AIRPLANE ENTERED A STALL/SPIN. THE PILOT TOOK OFF ON RUNWAY 26 WITH A LEFT QUARTERING TAIL WIND WITH TREES 60 FOOT TALL AT THE DEPARTURE END. A TAKE OFF ON RUNWAY 08 WOULD HAVE BEEN WITH A RIGHT QUARTERING HEAD WIND AND LOW TREES (APPROXIMATELY 20 TO 30 FEET TALL) ON THE DEPARTURE END.

THE ENGINE WAS STARTED AND OPERATED NORMAL WITH CORRECT FUEL PRESSURE. 20040810019009I	(-23) WHILE LANDING AT GCN, THE AIRCRAFT VEERED TO THE LEFT AND DEPARTED THE RUNWAY. THE AIRCRAFT THEN STRUCK A RUNWAY EDGE LIGHT WITH THE NOSE GEAR AND A FRANGIBLE TAXIWAY SIGN WITH THE RIGHT MAIN LANDING GEAR. WITNESSES WHO OBSERVED THE AIRCRAFT ON FINAL, STATED THAT THE NOSE GEAR APPEARED TO BE TURNED NEARLY 90 DEGREES TO THE DIRECTION OF FLIGHT. INSPECTION OF THE NOSE TIRE AT THE SCENE REVEALED CUPPING THAT APPEARED TO BE NEARLY 90 DEGREES TO THE DIRECTION OF LANDING. THE SWERVE MADE BY THE AIRCRAFT WAS HARD ENOUGH TO ROLL THE RIGHT MAIN TIRE OFF OF ITS RIM CAUSING IT TO DEFLATE. IT APPEARS THAT THIS INCIDENT WAS THE RESULT OF THREE INTERRELATED ISSUES. THE MAINTENANCE OF THE NOSE WHEEL STEERING CENTERING DEVICE AND INDICATOR; THE DESIGN OF THE NOSE WHEEL STEERING SYSTEM; AND INADEQUATE PILOT OPERATING PROCEDURES. AFTER RECOVERING THE AIRCRAFT, THE OPERATOR DISCOVERED THAT WITH THE COCKPIT NOSE WHEEL STEERING INDICATOR ALIGNED, THE NOSE WHEEL STEERING COLLAR DID NOT QUITE ALIGN WITH THE CENTERING TANG WHICH PREVENTED THE NOSE WHEEL FROM LOCKING IN THE CENTERED POSITION WHILE AIRBORNE. WHILE IT WAS CONFIRMED THAT THE CLEARANCES IN THE SYSTEM WERE WITHIN TOLERANCE, WHEN COMBINED,IN THIS CASE, THEY APPARENTLY PREVENTED THE NOSE WHEEL FROM BEING LOCKED IN THE CENTERED POSITION. THE OPERATOR HAS REVISED THEIR INSPECTION AND MAINTENANCE PROCEDURES IN AN EFFORT TO MAINTAIN TIGHTER TOLERANCES WITHIN THE NOSE WHEEL STEERING SYSTEM. REGARDING DESIGN OF THE NOSE WHEEL STEERING SYSTEM, THE HANDLE IS IN CLOSE PROXIMITY TO THE YOKE AND APPEARS CAPABLE OF BEING ACCIDENTALLY BUMPED. THIS WOULD CAUSE AN UNLATCHED NOSE WHEEL TO MOVE FROM A CENTERED POSITION AS ON THE INCIDENT AIRCRAFT. FINALLY, THE OPERATOR LACKED A PROCEDURE THAT WOULD ENSURE THAT THE NOSE WHEEL WAS, IN FACT, CENTERED AND LATCHED. THIS INCIDENT HAS BEEN RESOLVED BY THE PUBLICATION OF A NEW PILOT PROCEDURE TO BE ACCOMPLISHED BOTH AFTER TAKE-OFF AND BEFORE LANDING. THE PROCEDURE IS TO MOVE THE NOSE WHEEL STEERING LEVER UP AND DOWN IN ORDER TO FEEL THAT THE NOSE GEAR HAD MECHANICALLY LOCKED INTO THE CENTER POSITION.

THE FLIGHT DEPARTED THE KALISPELL CITY AIRPORT (S27) AT APPROXIMATELY 1200 MDT. SEVERAL WITNESSES IN THE AREA SUBMITTED ORAL AND WRITTEN STATEMENTS TO LAW ENFORCEMENT PERSONNEL.
